obstacles: Whole-head elevation can look like upper-jaw movement.
assessments.rationale: Anatomical joint geometry and kinematic evidence separate actual upper-jaw rotation from head movement, giving a decisive test.

assessments.operationalization: Compare histology and skeletal composition of dolphin vertebrae with mammalian bone and fish skeletal tissue.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: cetacean skeletal specimens

candidate_datasets.name: Digital Morphology
candidate_datasets.role: comparative vertebrate skeletal imaging

assessments.rationale: Dolphin skeletons are widely represented in public collections, and tissue identity is directly observable.

assessments.operationalization: Across cranial-appendage-bearing mammals, code solidity, branching, annual shedding and castration status for cervids and noncervids.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: comparative cranial appendage characters

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: cervid antler growth and shedding accounts

obstacles: Stag may mean red deer rather than all cervids.
Castration evidence is less systematically available.
assessments.rationale: The appendage traits and annual cycle are broadly documented, but the castration exception has thinner reusable data.

assessments.operationalization: Inspect distal digits of elephants and other toed animals for keratinous nails or hoof-like structures.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: 3D foot specimens across mammals

candidate_datasets.name: Digital Morphology
candidate_datasets.role: elephant pedal anatomy imaging

obstacles: Whether elephant hoof-like plates count as nails needs a criterion.
assessments.rationale: Specimen imaging directly documents elephant toenails and comparative digit coverings, making the anatomical claim decisively testable.

assessments.operationalization: Jointly code reproductive mode, limbs and integumentary covering across mammals, reptiles and fishes; search for violations of each universal.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: vertebrate integument and appendage phenotypes

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish scales and reproductive traits

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: comparative integument characters

obstacles: Hair, scute and scale homologies require explicit definitions.
assessments.rationale: Broad comparative resources cover all three clades and expose counterexamples, although harmonizing ancient categories reduces certainty.

assessments.operationalization: Use longitudinal calibrated microscopy of individual hairs to locate pigment loss along shafts and determine whether newly emerged grey hairs begin white.
obstacles: No known open longitudinal hair-level dataset.
Existing hair shafts cannot reveal when each segment changed colour.
assessments.rationale: The proposed chronology is measurable, but available images and cross-sectional studies do not provide the longitudinal, follicle-level observations required.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate alopecia prevalence by age, sex and castration status, and compare secondary-hair development after prepubertal castration.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Science Framework
candidate_datasets.role: public datasets from alopecia and endocrine studies where deposited

obstacles: Women can have several forms of alopecia.
Historical castration cohorts are rare and selected.
assessments.rationale: Large human studies resolve sex and age components, but open data on castration timing and later hair development are scarce.

assessments.operationalization: Code age-related plumage colour change across bird species and compare juvenile, adult and senescent common cranes.
obstacles: Age-labelled plumage observations are not standardized globally.
Moult and season confound age.
assessments.rationale: Public observations can identify counterexamples and characterize cranes, but a comprehensive age-controlled colour dataset is lacking.

assessments.operationalization: Randomize rams before mating to the candidate water versus control water and compare offspring coat-colour genotypes and phenotypes.
obstacles: No identified public dataset records paternal pre-mating water and lamb colour.
Parental coat-colour genetics is a major confound.
assessments.rationale: The causal prediction is experimentally crisp, but existing husbandry data do not contain the exposure and controls; new randomized data are required.

assessments.operationalization: Use staged embryo imaging and molecular markers to compare first detectable cardiac blood cells with whole-body tissue differentiation.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: developmental morphology specimens and image series

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: developmental anatomical phenotype annotations

obstacles: “First” depends on detection method and differentiation definition.
Coverage is concentrated in model vertebrates.
assessments.rationale: Developmental series can test selected vertebrates, but stage resolution and broad taxonomic coverage are insufficient for the full scope.

assessments.operationalization: Code internal and external viviparity, mammary glands and lactation across mammals, cetaceans, fishes and birds and test their association.

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: mammalian reproductive traits

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: mammary and lactation accounts

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish reproductive modes for comparison

obstacles: Some live-bearing fishes complicate ancient categories.
assessments.rationale: The mammalian component is comprehensively documented and comparison groups are well covered, allowing direct tests of both positive and negative clauses.

assessments.operationalization: Define thickness by viscosity or total solids, then compare standardized milk measurements for camel, human, donkey and cow.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Science Framework
candidate_datasets.role: public deposited food-composition datasets where available

obstacles: “Thickest” could mean viscosity, fat or total solids.
Lactation stage and processing alter measurements.
assessments.rationale: Milk composition data exist for all species, but are scattered and heterogeneous; the result depends materially on the chosen thickness metric.

assessments.operationalization: For semen samples, measure sinking or dissolution in standardized water and independently assay fertilization success; compare outcomes blinded.
obstacles: No known public dataset pairs this physical test with fertility.
Water chemistry and semen concentration alter behavior.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is direct, but the paired physical and fertility observations needed to assess it are not available as a public dataset.

assessments.operationalization: Count arms and sucker rows on specimens across octopus, squid and cuttlefish species, including Eledone.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: 3D cephalopod specimens

obstacles: Aristotle’s mollusc category is restricted to cephalopods.
assessments.rationale: These conspicuous characters are extensively catalogued and public specimen records can decisively test the universal and exception.

assessments.operationalization: Observe mating and inspect male arm morphology to identify hectocotylus use, position, colour and tip shape across octopus species.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: cephalopod anatomical specimens

obstacles: Arm numbering conventions differ.
The stated shape may apply only to a mapped species.
assessments.rationale: Reproductive behavior and hectocotylized arms are directly documented, permitting a strong test once species and arm numbering are fixed.

assessments.operationalization: Compile observations of defensive inking after standardized threats across octopuses, squids and cuttlefish, and compare discharge volume relative to body mass. Any non-inking species refutes the universal claim; consistently greatest relative volume in cuttlefish supports the comparison.
obstacles: Ink volume and eliciting threat are not standardized in broad databases.
The universal quantifier requires unusually complete taxonomic coverage.
assessments.rationale: Defensive inking and discharge amount are measurable, but observations are dispersed through species accounts and experiments. Existing evidence can test major clades and the cuttlefish comparison, not confidently every cephalopod.

assessments.operationalization: Count thoracic appendages, treating chelipeds as the first walking-leg pair, in identified spiny lobsters and true crabs. Ten appendages supports the claim, while a consistent different count refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: open specimen imagery and 3D media for appendage counts

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: modern taxonomy for spiny lobsters and brachyuran crabs

obstacles: Damaged museum specimens can be missing legs.
assessments.rationale: The characters are standard decapod anatomy and can be scored directly from abundant public specimen media and taxonomic descriptions. The result cleanly distinguishes ten limbs from alternative counts.

assessments.operationalization: Measure left and right chela dimensions in sexed Homarus specimens, define a preregistered equality tolerance, and estimate the frequency of symmetric animals by sex. Any verified equal-clawed individual refutes the absolute statement.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media usable for bilateral claw measurements

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: occurrence and taxonomic context for Homarus sampling

obstacles: Public images often omit sex and measurement scale.
Regenerated claws can confound innate asymmetry.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is precise and falsifiable, but no broad open table appears to pair sex with bilateral claw measurements. Public specimens and literature permit a substantial sample, though not a decisive census of both species and sexes.

assessments.operationalization: For a taxonomically broad sample of brachyuran specimens, score which chela is larger and test whether right-handed individuals exceed 50%. A majority on the right supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public crab specimen media for chela laterality

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: accepted brachyuran taxonomy

obstacles: Laterality varies strongly among crab families.
Images and specimens are not sampled randomly for handedness.
assessments.rationale: Laterality is straightforward to score, and a majority criterion is discriminating. Existing open media are biased and do not provide representative coverage of brachyurans, so only restricted taxonomic tests are currently feasible.

assessments.operationalization: Map 'stromboid testaceans' to gastropod taxa, score shell coiling as dextral or sinistral from specimens, and separately code locomotor direction relative to the spire. A sinistral member refutes the universal coiling statement.

candidate_datasets.name: MolluscaBase
candidate_datasets.role: accepted gastropod names and taxonomic scope

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: shell media for coiling direction

obstacles: The ancient category 'stromboid' has several modern interpretations.
Locomotor direction is rarely encoded in specimen datasets.
assessments.rationale: Shell handedness is easily resolved with public collections, including known exceptions to universal dextrality. The locomotion clause and ancient taxonomic boundary are much less directly represented, making the combined claim only partial.

assessments.operationalization: Identify the named predatory gastropods and compile observations or shell traces showing proboscis-associated drilling through prey shells. Repeated direct observations and diagnostic boreholes support the claim; absence of drilling with a different feeding mechanism refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: MolluscaBase
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic mapping of murex and trumpet-shell names

obstacles: Predatory drilling may involve the radula and accessory boring organ rather than the proboscis alone.
Behavioral evidence is spread across papers.
assessments.rationale: Drilled prey shells and feeding behavior are observable and strongly discriminating. Public databases establish taxa and ecology, while mechanism-specific data require literature compilation and may reveal that the stated anatomy is oversimplified.

assessments.operationalization: The anatomical resemblance and shell-occupying habit can be measured, but no observation uniquely decides whether those traits make the hermit crab 'intermediate' between Aristotle's kinds.
obstacles: 'Intermediate' is a classificatory judgment without a quantitative decision rule.
The compared ancient categories do not correspond to sister modern taxa.
assessments.rationale: The component facts are empirically documentable, but the central conclusion depends on Aristotle's classification. Different weighting of morphology and habit can yield either classification without any new observation deciding between them.

assessments.operationalization: Mouth position, anus position and benthic feeding can be recorded, but those observations do not distinguish adaptive final placement from a non-teleological developmental explanation.
obstacles: The phrase 'because it is best suited' supplies no rival-sensitive prediction.
The anatomical fact used as evidence is also what the explanation seeks to explain.
assessments.rationale: Existing data readily confirm the orientation and feeding substrate, but mere fit does not test the final-cause explanation. No stated measurable consequence separates that explanation from developmental or phylogenetic alternatives.

assessments.operationalization: Count gonads in dissected or imaged sea-urchin specimens across representative taxa and developmental anomalies. Five in every normal specimen supports the statement; any authenticated normal specimen with another count refutes 'always'.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: 3D and specimen media showing echinoid internal anatomy

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic coverage of Echinoidea

obstacles: Abnormal individuals require a prespecified inclusion rule.
assessments.rationale: Gonad number is a standard and conspicuous echinoid character. Public anatomical resources plus taxonomic descriptions provide broad coverage, and a non-five count gives a direct falsification.

assessments.operationalization: Measure solid and dissolved waste release from identified sea anemones while feeding, and compare presence of egestion or nitrogenous excretion with plants under a stated definition. Detecting waste products refutes the no-excretion clause.

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: modern taxonomic mapping of Actiniaria

obstacles: 'Excretion' could mean feces, metabolic excretion, or a dedicated outlet.
Physiological flux data are scattered across experiments.
assessments.rationale: Waste release is measurable, but the ancient term is ambiguous and the plant resemblance is qualitative. Existing physiological literature can resolve particular species and definitions, not the full category as phrased.

assessments.operationalization: Define a standardized bisection plane and survival interval, then compare post-bisection survival across insect orders, body sizes and temperatures. Failure to survive in warm, sufficiently large insects would refute the qualified universal.
obstacles: No broad public dataset records survival after experimental bisection.
The exceptions 'cold by nature' and 'chill quickly' are not operationally specified.
A representative test would require new experiments.
assessments.rationale: The survival outcome is testable after substantial clarification, but occurrence and trait databases do not contain the required intervention. Isolated reports cannot adequately cover the stated scope of all insects.

assessments.operationalization: Map two-winged insects to Diptera and inspect adult posterior abdominal anatomy across families for a true sting. One dipteran with a homologous posterior sting refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public insect specimen imagery and scans

candidate_datasets.name: Catalogue of Life
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic sampling frame for Diptera

obstacles: Piercing ovipositors and biting mouthparts must be distinguished from stings.
Public anatomy media are uneven across dipteran families.
assessments.rationale: The statement has a clear anatomical interpretation and a decisive counterexample criterion. Existing collections can cover many families, but proving absence across the enormous order remains limited by uneven anatomical annotation.

assessments.operationalization: Code cicada mouthparts, food sources from feeding observations or plant-DNA/chemical evidence, and gut or waste contents. Functional mouthparts, feeding on xylem rather than dew, or excretion refutes the corresponding clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media for cicada mouthpart anatomy

obstacles: No single open dataset joins mouthpart, diet and excretion observations.
The claim combines three distinct propositions.
assessments.rationale: Each component has direct observable consequences and extensive existing evidence. Public data can strongly test representative cicadas, though compiling adequate species-level coverage and gut physiology requires literature extraction.

assessments.operationalization: A test would require a non-circular criterion for individuating senses; without one, detecting magnetoreception, electroreception or proprioception can be redescribed as touch or as a new sense.
obstacles: The number depends on how sensory modalities are defined and grouped.
The phrase 'special sense' lacks an empirical identity criterion.
assessments.rationale: Animals have measurable sensory channels beyond the traditional five, but whether each counts as a separate sense is conceptual. Data alone cannot settle the asserted total without first choosing a taxonomy of senses.

assessments.operationalization: Use histology and 3D anatomical images of Talpa eyes to score external visibility, size and presence of canonical ocular structures. Missing canonical parts or exposed normal-sized eyes refute the stated anatomy.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public 3D and specimen media for mammalian cranial anatomy

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts and referenced anatomical descriptions

obstacles: 'All parts' needs a defined list of ocular structures.
assessments.rationale: Mole eye reduction is standard comparative anatomy with abundant archived specimens and published histology. The core claims of hidden position, reduction and structural completeness can be directly checked with existing material.

assessments.operationalization: Compile auditory and olfactory organs and behavioral or electrophysiological responses to controlled sound and odor stimuli across fishes. Responses above controls support hearing and smell; anatomical evidence tests the 'no visible organs' qualifier.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: species biology and sensory ecology references for fishes

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: fish anatomical scans showing internal sensory structures

obstacles: Startle to galley noise alone may also involve vibration or lateral-line detection.
assessments.rationale: Hearing and olfaction have standard behavioral and physiological assays, and extensive existing fish data. Multiple independent response measures distinguish these senses from a generic startle response.

assessments.operationalization: Modern invertebrate diversity can be assigned to Aristotle's four bins only after choosing definitions; no observation determines that these rather than another set are the correct genera.
obstacles: The four kinds are an ancient classificatory scheme, not an exhaustive measurable hypothesis.
Modern taxa such as flatworms and cnidarians do not map uniquely to the bins.
assessments.rationale: Species traits and phylogeny could expose omissions, but 'with very few exceptions' has no threshold and the categories are stipulated. The core claim concerns classification and cannot be resolved independently of a chosen scheme.

assessments.operationalization: Define voice as actively generated communication sound, then code lung presence, sound-production anatomy and recordings across animals. A lungless animal producing such sound without a pharynx refutes the universal mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public animal sound recordings

obstacles: 'Voice' can be restricted by definition to pulmonary phonation.
Sound archives do not systematically encode production mechanisms.
assessments.rationale: The claim becomes testable under a behaviorally neutral definition of voice, and public recordings include many lungless sound producers. Mechanism and anatomy must be compiled separately, so broad resolution is possible but not turnkey.

assessments.operationalization: Measure gas exchange and ventilatory airflow through insect spiracles and tracheae, and identify sound-production mechanisms. Demonstrated active respiratory ventilation refutes 'no insect breathes,' while mechanism data test whether sound depends on expelled air.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: insect anatomical media for tracheal and sound-producing structures

obstacles: 'Breathes' may mean lung breathing rather than any respiration.
Physiological measurements are scattered by species.
assessments.rationale: Gas exchange and ventilation are directly measurable and extensively studied, but ancient terminology creates an interpretation choice. Existing data resolve representative mechanisms well, with incomplete order-wide coverage.

assessments.operationalization: Predefine language by measurable features such as compositional syntax, displaced reference and open-ended productivity, then code controlled communication studies in humans and other mammals. A nonhuman system meeting all criteria refutes uniqueness under that definition.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public comparative animal vocal recordings

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: large public collection of animal vocalizations

obstacles: No consensus definition cleanly separates language from complex communication.
Recordings alone rarely establish semantics or syntax.
Controlled cognition data are sparse and heterogeneous.
assessments.rationale: Some consequences of the uniqueness claim can be tested, but the verdict depends heavily on a prior definition of language. Existing recordings and experiments test restricted features rather than the full philosophical contrast.

assessments.operationalization: Compare songs of cross-fostered or acoustically isolated juveniles with tutors and genetic parents, and quantify geographic song variation. Tutor matching and locality effects beyond genetic structure support learned modification.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: georeferenced bird recordings for dialect analysis

candidate_datasets.name: Xeno-canto
candidate_datasets.role: public georeferenced bird-song recordings

obstacles: Archive recordings alone do not identify cross-fostering histories.
assessments.rationale: Vocal learning has standard acoustic comparisons and extensive archived recordings plus existing cross-fostering studies. Geographic variation and tutor effects can be tested independently with current resources.

assessments.operationalization: Use REM-like physiology, sleep vocalization or replay-related neural activity as preregistered proxies for dreaming in named mammals. Presence supports dream-like experience, while absence does not by itself refute subjective dreaming.

candidate_datasets.name: OpenNeuro
candidate_datasets.role: public neurophysiology datasets, including sleep studies where available

obstacles: Dreaming is subjective and cannot be directly reported by nonhuman animals.
Physiological proxies do not uniquely imply dream experience.
Open comparative coverage is poor outside laboratory species.
assessments.rationale: Existing sleep physiology can test dream-like neural states in several mammals, but the universal claim and subjective interpretation remain underdetermined. Behavioral barking is suggestive rather than decisive.

assessments.operationalization: Define sleep by reversible quiescence, elevated arousal threshold and homeostatic rebound, then compile duration measurements for fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans. Sleep in each clade supports the first clause; durations comparable to or longer than other animals refute 'very short'.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish behavior and ecology records

obstacles: Sleep criteria differ among distant phyla.
Duration data are concentrated in a few model species.
'Very short' lacks a numerical comparator.
assessments.rationale: Behavioral sleep is operationalizable across these clades, and existing studies cover representative species. Broad taxonomic coverage and the vague duration comparison prevent resolution as stated.

assessments.operationalization: Analyze tagged or video-recorded cetacean sleep bouts for blowhole position relative to the surface, breathing and fin movement. Submerged sleep or immobile sleep in a blowhole-bearing species refutes the corresponding universal clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: public animal-borne movement datasets where cetacean records are shared

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic and occurrence context for cetacean coverage

obstacles: Sleep state is difficult to infer from location tags.
Fine-scale public biologging data cover few cetacean species.
assessments.rationale: The predicted posture and breathing are observable, and existing biologging and captive studies test dolphins and some whales. Public data do not adequately span all blowhole-bearing animals or consistently label sleep.

assessments.operationalization: Map sessile animals and testaceans to modern taxa and code gonochorism, hermaphroditism and asexual reproduction from reproductive records. Any sessile or shelled taxon with separate males and females refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic mapping of marine sessile and shelled animals

obstacles: Aristotle's 'testaceans' includes several unrelated modern phyla.
Sex systems can vary within species.
assessments.rationale: Sex system is a standard species trait, and public records contain decisive counterexamples across the relevant groups. Ancient category mapping adds some uncertainty but does not prevent testing the universal statement.

assessments.operationalization: Inspect sexed Anguilla specimens and reproductive datasets for ovaries, testes, gametes, spawning and offspring. Any verified male, female, egg or successful reproduction refutes the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: eel reproduction, sex and life-history records

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: eel occurrence and life-stage context

obstacles: Spawning occurs in remote oceanic areas, so direct observations are rare.
assessments.rationale: Sex, gonads and eggs are direct measurable variables, with extensive modern data for Anguilla. Existing anatomical and reproductive evidence can decisively resolve the assertion despite elusive natural spawning.

assessments.operationalization: Resolve each ancient fish name to candidate species, then compile sex ratios, gonadal sex and egg-bearing observations. A confirmed male or a non-egg-bearing mature individual refutes 'always found with eggs' for that mapping.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: modern fish taxonomy and reproductive biology

obstacles: Psetta and erythrinus have disputed modern identifications.
Occurrence records do not usually include sex or gonadal state.
Season strongly affects egg presence.
assessments.rationale: The biological prediction is clear once taxa are fixed, but name mapping is uncertain and relevant reproductive records are scattered. Existing data can test plausible candidate species, not uniquely resolve the historical taxa.

assessments.operationalization: Join adult body mass, sex and longevity across mammals and compare sex ratios of those traits with analogous size data for fishes, insects, reptiles, spiders and frogs using phylogenetic models. Directional majorities support each 'general rule'.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: sex-specific and species-level longevity records

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open animal trait records including body size and life history

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish maximum size and reproductive traits

obstacles: Sex-specific longevity is much sparser than body size.
The ancient groups mix many clades with different patterns.
Captive longevity can bias sex comparisons.
assessments.rationale: Sexual size dimorphism is well represented in public trait data, while sex-specific lifespan is less complete. Existing resources support broad comparative tests but not equally adequate resolution of every taxonomic and longevity clause.

assessments.operationalization: For insects and internal parasites reported to arise from decay or secretions, use life-cycle, parentage and genomic evidence to determine whether individuals derive from eggs, larvae or propagules of conspecific parents. Demonstrated parental origin refutes spontaneous generation.

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: public DNA barcode records linking insect and parasite life stages

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public sequence and organism records for life-cycle identification

obstacles: The claim's historical examples are not enumerated species by species.
assessments.rationale: Spontaneous generation makes clear, strongly discriminating predictions about ancestry and life cycles. Existing developmental, genetic and rearing data can resolve the proposed mechanism for the relevant modern taxa without new collection.

assessments.operationalization: Compile sex-specific mature body lengths and masses for sharks, rays, skates and other fishes, then estimate the proportion of species with female-biased size. Female-biased values in a majority support each generalization.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish size, sex and life-history records

candidate_datasets.name: Shark-References
candidate_datasets.role: public bibliographic and biological records for chondrichthyans

obstacles: Sex-specific maximum size is missing for many species.
Size metric and maturity stage require harmonization.
assessments.rationale: Sexual size dimorphism is directly measurable and well documented for many fishes. Public coverage is substantial but incomplete and biased toward exploited species, limiting a whole-class majority estimate.

assessments.operationalization: Inspect sexed chondrichthyan specimens for paired pelvic claspers adjacent to the cloaca. Their presence in males and absence in females across sampled species supports the sex difference; any contrary anatomy refutes universality.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public specimen images and scans of chondrichthyans

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: species taxonomy and reproductive anatomy references

obstacles: Immature male claspers can be inconspicuous.
assessments.rationale: Claspers are a standard, externally visible sexually dimorphic character of male chondrichthyans. Existing specimens and descriptions provide broad, decisive coverage using a simple analysis.

assessments.operationalization: Code presence, location and homology of testes and sperm ducts in male fishes and snakes from dissections and anatomical images. Any gonadal structure homologous to a testis refutes the no-testicle clause; paired seasonal sperm ducts test the second clause.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public anatomical scans and specimen media

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish reproductive anatomy and breeding records

obstacles: Aristotle may use 'testicles' narrowly for externally pendant testes.
Duct terminology differs across vertebrate groups.
assessments.rationale: Modern gonadal homology and duct anatomy are directly observable in extensive archived material. The main uncertainty is terminological rather than a lack of data, and explicit definitions permit a decisive test.

assessments.operationalization: Score testis position in male birds, reptiles and amphibians from dissections and imaging. Internal testes across these footed oviparous groups support the claim; an external testis in a member refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public vertebrate anatomy images and 3D scans

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: referenced reproductive anatomy accounts

obstacles: The boundary of 'footed' needs rules for limbless descendants.
assessments.rationale: Testis location is standard vertebrate anatomy with broad existing specimen coverage. A simple taxonomically stratified review can confirm or refute the stated pattern.

assessments.operationalization: Code urinary bladder presence across oviparous birds, reptiles, amphibians and fishes, with tortoises identified separately. Any non-tortoise oviparous animal with a bladder refutes the single-exception claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public anatomical media for urinary systems

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: comparative vertebrate anatomy accounts and references

obstacles: Homology of bladder-like structures must be defined across vertebrates.
assessments.rationale: Bladder presence is an ordinary anatomical character and public comparative material includes the named groups. Counterexamples or broad support can be found with standard review and imaging methods.

assessments.operationalization: House virgin female partridges with randomized exposure to male odor downwind, male calls, overhead airflow, physical mating or no male, then verify fertilization genetically. Fertile eggs without sperm transfer would support the claim.
obstacles: No known public dataset records controlled non-contact impregnation treatments.
Prior sperm storage and unnoticed copulation must be excluded.
A decisive test requires new controlled breeding experiments.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is clear and experimentally discriminating, but ordinary breeding or occurrence datasets cannot test it. Existing general reproductive knowledge is not a substitute for treatment-level partridge data.

assessments.operationalization: Code mating posture, contact point and sperm-transfer organ from videos and descriptions of octopuses, cuttlefish and squids. Transfer via hectocotylized arms rather than mouth union refutes the proposed common mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic sampling frame for cephalopod groups

obstacles: Mating videos are not systematically archived by species.
Arm interlacing can look like mouth-to-mouth union without showing sperm transfer.
assessments.rationale: The behavior and anatomy have direct observational tests, and extensive existing accounts cover common species. Public structured data are less complete across all three groups, so the universal wording is only partly resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Use genital morphology and mating observations to identify which sex intromits a structure in flies, cantharid beetles and a broader insect sample. Male intromission in any included insect refutes the general reversal.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

Behavioral data are sparse across insect diversity.
assessments.rationale: Direction of intromission is measurable and counterexamples are decisive. Existing morphology and observations test selected orders, but no comprehensive open behavioral dataset spans insects.

assessments.operationalization: For Mediterranean animals, infer breeding dates from reproductive observations and test whether species-level peaks cluster in spring more than other seasons. A preregistered majority threshold would define support for 'almost all'.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish spawning seasons

obstacles: 'Almost all' and 'spring' require explicit thresholds.
Reproductive annotations are missing from most occurrence records.
Seasonality varies with latitude and climate.

candidate_datasets.name: eBird

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open animal life-history traits

candidate_datasets.role: mammalian reproductive and life-history records

Annual brood number changes with latitude and resource conditions.
Superfetation can be confused with superfecundation.

assessments.operationalization: Resolve pelamys to Atlantic bluefin tuna juveniles or bonito, then map georeferenced spawning-stage adults, eggs and larvae. Verified spawning outside the Black Sea refutes exclusivity for the relevant mapping.

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System

assessments.rationale: The variables and temporal prediction are clear, and existing observations address common octopus species. Data are scattered and do not cover the broad unqualified taxon adequately.

assessments.operationalization: For Paracentrotus lividus, model repeated gonad index against season, water temperature and lunar phase while controlling site and size. Persistent positive full-moon and warm-weather effects support those clauses; seasonal absence of gonads refutes 'never without'.

Lunar phase is confounded with tides and sampling schedules.
The species identification is probable rather than certain.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate annual successful brood counts from repeated nest records for wild birds, with separate estimates for swallows and blackbirds. One brood in a majority and two in the named exceptions support the statement.

candidate_datasets.name: NestWatch

candidate_datasets.name: eBird
candidate_datasets.role: dated breeding observations across bird species

obstacles: Repeated broods by the same pair are difficult to identify from opportunistic records.
Brood number varies geographically and between years.
assessments.rationale: Breeding attempts are standard observations with large current monitoring resources. Named species can be tested well, but estimating a representative rule for all wild birds requires individual-level linkage often absent from open records.

assessments.operationalization: Map the four Greek columbids to candidate modern species and compare adult body mass and length distributions. The stated rank order is supported if species means and distributions follow it; reversed comparisons refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: AVONET

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open body-size traits for animals

assessments.operationalization: Within individuals, compare fertilization success and offspring or egg size from the first mature ejaculate or clutch with later ones, stratified by taxon. Equal or better first reproductive output refutes the asserted universal deterioration.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public research datasets that may contain clutch order and reproductive outcomes

obstacles: 'Earliest semen' is ambiguous between puberty, season and mating sequence.
Longitudinal first-reproduction data are sparse and dispersed.
The claim spans very different reproductive systems.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate age distributions for spermarche, viable sperm production and achieved paternity in male humans. Medians or stated percentiles near fourteen and twenty-one support the two age claims; materially different distributions refute them.

candidate_datasets.name: Demographic and Health Surveys

assessments.operationalization: Extract fundamental frequency from sexed, age-labeled recordings within species and fit phylogenetically structured sex and age effects. Predominantly higher female and juvenile pitch supports the general rule.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public identified animal sounds

Fundamental frequency depends on call type and behavioral context.

assessments.operationalization: Measure fundamental frequency from comparable calls of adult cows, bulls and calves, controlling breed and context. Lower female than male and lower calf than adult frequencies support the two reversals.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public cattle vocal recordings

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: additional public mammal recordings

Call types differ between calves and adults.

assessments.operationalization: Compare acoustic pitch and prespecified secondary sexual traits in intact males, castrated males and females, controlling age and species. Movement of castrated males toward female trait values supports the specific measurable consequences.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Sound Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public mammal vocal recordings where sex and condition are documented

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public experimental and veterinary datasets on castration effects

Open matched datasets are uncommon.

assessments.operationalization: Analyze mating- or ovulation-dated canine pregnancies for birth timing and neonatal survival. The gestation distribution tests 60–63 days, and surviving litters born before 60 days refute the survival exception.

candidate_datasets.name: VetCompass
candidate_datasets.role: large veterinary clinical data resource for dogs

assessments.operationalization: Estimate sex-specific horse lifespan and age-specific reproductive success from pedigree and longevity records. Means or survival quantiles near 35 and over 40, with reproduction near the lifespan limit, support the statement.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database

candidate_datasets.name: Domestic Animal Diversity Information System

assessments.operationalization: Use age-specific births by maternal and paternal age to estimate typical and upper reproductive limits, distinguishing biological capability from observed reproduction. Frequent births beyond the proposed limits refute them; rare tails test the stated maxima.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Fertility Database

candidate_datasets.name: Demographic and Health Surveys

assessments.operationalization: Compile breeding records for dromedaries with conception and birth dates and litter size. A gestation distribution centered near twelve months and singleton births support the claim; verified twins refute 'never'.

candidate_datasets.name: Domestic Animal Diversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: public information on domestic camel breeds

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: camel reproductive life-history records and references

candidate_datasets.name: Species360

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database

assessments.operationalization: For Bolinus brandaris and Hexaplex trunculus, compare known-age or mark-recaptured lifespan with counts of shell growth intervals validated against annual chronology. Agreement at one interval per year and survival near six years supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MolluscaBase

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: co-occurrence and distribution records for Pinna and commensals

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems

assessments.operationalization: Compile validated lifespan distributions for squid, cuttlefish and octopus species and estimate the fraction surviving beyond one year. A substantial frequency of multi-year species refutes the broad 'few exceptions' statement.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive

assessments.operationalization: Compile life cycles of human tapeworms, roundworms and pinworms, identifying whether eggs produced by intestinal adults develop into conspecific descendants. Viable conspecific offspring refute the no-propagation claim.
