candidate_datasets.role: public birth data including plurality

obstacles: Extreme historical cases require verification of live versus still births.
Some public files top-code very high plurality.
assessments.rationale: Plurality is routinely recorded in large birth registries, making the maximum claim directly testable. Verified sextuplet and higher-order deliveries can serve as decisive counterexamples without estimating a population rate.

assessments.operationalization: Define acceptance as observed receptive mating behavior and compare its rate during pregnancy among women, mares, hares and representative other mammals.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open animal behavioral and reproduction study datasets

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed Central
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative reproductive-behavior literature

obstacles: Human sexual behavior is not directly comparable to animal estrus.
Pregnancy-stage mating behavior is not broadly standardized.
The superlative 'most inclined' requires exhaustive coverage.
assessments.rationale: The claim can be operationalized behaviorally, but comparable cross-species data are sparse and conceptually heterogeneous. Existing studies can test individual taxa and exceptions, not the full ranking.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate age distributions for natural menopause and childbirth, testing modal cessation near forty, an upper limit near fifty and absence of births beyond fifty.

candidate_datasets.name: DHS Program
candidate_datasets.role: international birth histories and menopause-related survey measures

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: maternal age in public birth records

obstacles: Assisted reproduction complicates the relation between menopause and childbirth.
Survey-defined menopause can be affected by surgery or contraception.
assessments.rationale: Menopause and maternal age are standard variables in large public datasets. The age distribution and claimed hard upper bound can both be tested directly, with sensitivity analyses for assisted conception.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate paternity and birth counts by paternal age, testing continued fatherhood through ages sixty and seventy while distinguishing sexual function from proven fertility.

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: public birth records containing paternal age

candidate_datasets.name: DHS Program
candidate_datasets.role: international male fertility and birth-history data

obstacles: Paternity at a given age does not measure general sexual competence.
Paternal age is missing from some birth records.
assessments.rationale: Large birth datasets readily establish whether men father children at sixty and seventy and estimate frequency. The broader sexual-competence component requires survey or clinical proxies but is also widely measured.

assessments.operationalization: Separate inherited genetic disorders from acquired scars, then compare parent-child concordance using pedigrees, diagnoses and image-derived marks.

candidate_datasets.name: dbGaP
candidate_datasets.role: genotype-phenotype family studies, many requiring controlled access

obstacles: Lameness and blindness have both inherited and acquired causes.
Scars are acquired and are not coded in most pedigrees.
Many family datasets are controlled rather than openly downloadable.
assessments.rationale: Heritable deformities are strongly testable with established pedigree and genetic resources. The assertion that acquired marks such as scars are transmitted needs rare linked observations and is not supported by a broad public dataset.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify facial or trait resemblance across three-generation pedigrees and test whether grandchildren can resemble grandparents more than their intervening parent.

candidate_datasets.name: dbGaP
candidate_datasets.role: multigenerational genotype-phenotype studies

candidate_datasets.name: Open Humans
candidate_datasets.role: participant-contributed public personal and genomic data

obstacles: Resemblance requires specified traits or image metrics.
Multigenerational identifiable images are privacy-sensitive.
Most dbGaP individual data require authorization.
assessments.rationale: Mendelian segregation and multigenerational phenotype data make skipped resemblance directly testable for defined traits. Privacy limits some access, but existing data and standard genetic methods are sufficient for resolution.

assessments.operationalization: Define comparable embryonic processes and attachment structures, then map yolk-sac, placenta and umbilical or vitelline connections across representative animal phyla.

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon
candidate_datasets.role: cross-species anatomy ontology for homologous developmental structures

obstacles: 'Develop in the same way' is too broad without chosen homologous stages.
Many animals lack a navel-like structure.
Coverage across all animal phyla is uneven.
assessments.rationale: Attachment structures can be compared using anatomy ontologies and developmental data, and counterexamples are accessible. The overarching sameness claim is underspecified and cannot be resolved as a single proposition.

assessments.operationalization: Compile fetal presentation near term and presentation at delivery across viviparous species, testing the universal head-first assertion and the claimed prenatal turn.

candidate_datasets.name: National Vital Statistics System
candidate_datasets.role: human birth presentation and delivery records

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed Central
candidate_datasets.role: open veterinary obstetric studies across mammals

obstacles: Presentation terminology differs across taxa.
Broad individual-level veterinary data are scattered.
Tail-first delivery may be normal in some species.
assessments.rationale: Birth presentation is routinely recorded in humans and veterinary medicine. The universal wording is decisively testable with documented normal posterior presentations even without complete coverage of every viviparous animal.

assessments.operationalization: Count arteries and veins in umbilical or yolk-sac connections from cattle, smaller mammals and chicken embryos, then test whether vessel number follows body size.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public anatomical imaging across vertebrates

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public embryo imaging datasets

obstacles: Bird yolk-sac vessels are not anatomically identical to a mammalian umbilical cord.
Vessel count changes across developmental stages.
Size categories are vague.
assessments.rationale: Vessel number is direct and visible in existing embryological images and anatomical literature. Homology and stage must be standardized, but the numeric size rule can be clearly confirmed or refuted.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate age and order of primary-tooth eruption from pediatric cohorts, then test any association with measured breast-milk temperature.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
candidate_datasets.role: public dental examination and age data

candidate_datasets.name: DHS Program
candidate_datasets.role: international child health and feeding data

obstacles: Milk temperature is rarely measured and 'warmer' may be metaphorical.
Cross-sectional dental exams interval-censor eruption age.
assessments.rationale: Timing and order of tooth eruption are well covered in public pediatric data and resolve the main claim. The milk-temperature mechanism lacks a standard variable and is only weakly assessable from existing resources.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate menstrual resumption as a function of exclusive and partial breastfeeding duration, while testing the proposed general suppression and documented exceptions.

candidate_datasets.name: DHS Program
candidate_datasets.role: international breastfeeding, postpartum amenorrhea and birth-history data

obstacles: Lactation intensity and supplementation strongly affect amenorrhea.
The moisture-allocation explanation is not directly represented in surveys.
assessments.rationale: Breastfeeding and postpartum amenorrhea are jointly measured in large public surveys, providing a direct test of the generalization and exceptions. The physiological explanation requires separate endocrine evidence but has measurable alternatives.

assessments.operationalization: Define behavioral measures for fear, aggression, affiliative behavior and problem solving, then estimate their presence and cross-species continuity across sampled animals and humans.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal QTLdb
candidate_datasets.role: public behavioral trait records for domesticated animals

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative animal cognition and behavior datasets

obstacles: Psychical qualities are anthropomorphic and multidimensional.
'Traces' makes nearly any behavior compatible.
Most animals have never been tested comparably.
assessments.rationale: Individual capacities can be operationalized with modern behavioral assays, but the very broad analogical claim has weak falsification criteria. Existing data can resolve selected qualities and taxa only.

assessments.operationalization: No unique dataset analysis can decide whether a chosen living/nonliving boundary is 'sharp'; trait matrices could only display gradients under a prespecified philosophical definition.
obstacles: Life and animal boundaries are classification choices.
Intermediate morphology does not by itself make a boundary impossible.
The proposed gradual order lacks a defined metric.
assessments.rationale: Data can document mixtures of traits in sponges, ascidians and other organisms, but every pattern remains compatible with multiple definitions of life and animality. The claim's central conclusion is conceptual rather than a discriminating empirical prediction.

assessments.operationalization: Relate standardized cognition or memory scores to duration of postnatal association and frequency of social interaction across species, controlling lifespan and developmental mode.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative cognition and parental-care datasets

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: developmental and reproductive covariates across vertebrates

obstacles: Comparable intelligence scores are unavailable for most taxa.
Parental association reflects ecology and development as well as cognition.
Memory and sociality are distinct constructs.
assessments.rationale: Parental-care duration is measurable, and selected comparative cognition datasets allow a restricted correlation test. Coverage and confounding are too severe for the general causal ranking.

assessments.operationalization: For each named taxon, verify respiratory organs, surfacing intervals, response to prevented air access, and breeding habitat.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public species accounts for respiration and reproduction

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: movement and dive records for aquatic air-breathing animals

obstacles: Frogs and some turtles can exchange gases through skin or cloaca.
Breeding habitat varies among species within the named groups.
assessments.rationale: Respiration, surfacing and breeding habitats are standard natural-history variables with broad public documentation. The compound universal is resolvable, including clear exceptions to simplified drowning or land-breeding language.

assessments.operationalization: Combine cetacean anatomy, dive records, bycatch mortality and sleep observations to test lung breathing, suffocation in nets, out-of-water survival and breathing during rest.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: cetacean movement and dive studies

candidate_datasets.name: OBIS-SEAMAP
candidate_datasets.role: public marine megavertebrate observations and survey data

obstacles: Out-of-water survival depends on species and conditions.
Sleep posture is difficult to observe in wild dolphins.
Bycatch records may not distinguish cause of death.
assessments.rationale: The respiratory anatomy and need to surface are directly established, while tracking and bycatch data address behavior and suffocation. Some duration and sleep details are less comprehensively sampled but remain testable.

assessments.operationalization: Measure water flow, oxygen uptake and heat exchange across fish gills, and separately test whether cetacean blowholes admit water during prey capture.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish respiratory physiology and ecology

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed Central
candidate_datasets.role: open gill physiology and cetacean respiratory anatomy studies

obstacles: Cooling and oxygen uptake occur simultaneously and need causal separation.
The claim incorrectly groups gills and blowholes under water intake.
Physiological datasets are species-specific.
assessments.rationale: Existing physiology can distinguish respiratory gas exchange from thermoregulation and test blowhole anatomy. The broad proposed common purpose is only partially comparable across the two very different systems.

assessments.operationalization: Map cordylus to candidate salamanders and compare adult respiratory organs, limb-supported terrestrial locomotion and feeding habitat.

candidate_datasets.name: AmphibiaWeb
candidate_datasets.role: public amphibian species accounts, life histories and morphology

obstacles: The ancient animal may be a larva, neotenic adult or different amphibian.
Gill retention and terrestrial activity vary by life stage.
The uniqueness claim requires exhaustive animal coverage.
assessments.rationale: Candidate taxa have documented respiratory anatomy and habitat use, enabling tests under each mapping. Identity uncertainty and the 'only known animal' superlative prevent a single definitive assessment.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify phenotypic changes after castration and relate experimentally measured embryonic gonadal or sex-determining changes to later sexual phenotype.

candidate_datasets.name: Mouse Genome Informatics
candidate_datasets.role: public mouse genotype and developmental phenotype data

candidate_datasets.name: Animal QTLdb
candidate_datasets.role: livestock traits including reproductive and castration-associated phenotypes

obstacles: 'Minute organ' and 'female form' are vague.
Castration effects and embryonic sex determination are distinct mechanisms.
A slight organ-size change is not a general sex-determination rule.
assessments.rationale: Existing veterinary and model-organism data can quantify many castration and sex-development effects. The broad principle and the proposed organ-size decision mechanism require substantial interpretation and cannot be tested as one coherent causal claim.

assessments.operationalization: Submerge sealed, weighed thin wax vessels in seawater for twenty-four hours and assay recovered internal water volume and salinity against controls.
obstacles: No known public dataset records this exact experiment.
Vessel sealing, wax permeability and contamination must be controlled.
Running the simple experiment would constitute new data collection.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is exceptionally clear and a standard salinity assay would decide it. However, the task concerns existing datasets, and none is known to contain replicated measurements of this exact wax-vessel setup.

assessments.operationalization: Compile diet and stomach-content records for fishes, coding conspecific predation and testing both its universality and absence in Mugilidae.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish diet, food items and ecology records

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: public species-interaction records including predation

obstacles: Absence of recorded cannibalism is not proof of absence.
Diet sampling is sparse for many fishes.
Life-stage cannibalism may be underidentified.
assessments.rationale: The universal assertion can be refuted by well-sampled species lacking cannibalism or by documented mullet cannibalism. Existing diet and interaction resources support these tests, though not an exhaustive proof of absence for every fish.

assessments.operationalization: Inspect comparative fish anatomy for an esophagus between pharynx and stomach and distinguish true stomach eversion from regurgitation during prey capture.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public three-dimensional fish anatomical specimens

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish morphology and feeding biology

obstacles: Digestive anatomy varies greatly among fishes.
Some fishes lack a differentiated stomach but still have an esophagus.
assessments.rationale: The presence and position of an esophagus are directly visible in extensive comparative anatomy. Existing specimens and literature also separate stomach eversion from ordinary regurgitation, making the universal claim decisively testable.

assessments.operationalization: Define rumination-like oral reprocessing from feeding video, then compare its occurrence in Sparisoma cretense with a broad sample of other fishes. Repeated post-ingestion chewing in only the focal species would support the claim; any documented counterexample would refute uniqueness.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: species identities, diets and referenced accounts of feeding behaviour

obstacles: Chewing the cud is an analogy rather than a standard fish-behaviour variable.
Existing behavioural coverage is sparse across fishes.
assessments.rationale: The focal behaviour can be defined from observations, but the universal uniqueness claim requires exceptionally broad coverage. FishBase and the literature can test the focal species and locate counterexamples, not establish absence in every other fish.

assessments.operationalization: Compile validated ages of European eels from otolith readings and tagged individuals and test whether observed lifespans include seven to eight years. Such records confirm possibility, while a well-covered lifespan distribution excluding that range would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: European eel longevity and age records with literature sources

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: validated longevity records

obstacles: Wild age estimates depend on otolith interpretation.
assessments.rationale: Age and lifespan are standard variables and the claim only asserts that some eels reach this age. Multiple mature databases and extensive eel studies make a direct, rapid test possible.

assessments.operationalization: Map the listed raptors to modern taxa, code diet and documented ingestion of grain or bread, and test the two universal statements. Any non-carnivorous species or verified swallowing event refutes the relevant statement.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: open species interaction and feeding records

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public media documenting bird feeding behaviour

obstacles: Inability to swallow is rarely measured.
Crooked talons does not define one modern clade.
assessments.rationale: Diet is well documented, and public observations can readily produce counterexamples. The physiological inability claim is much less systematically represented, so the conjunction is only partly resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Code direct drinking events and water intake rates for raptor species from observational records and captive studies. Any routine drinking refutes 'never', while comparative rates can test 'very little'.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: searchable public bird videos and photographs that can document drinking

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: public observations and media of raptors

obstacles: Non-observation cannot establish that drinking never occurs.
Media are strongly opportunistic.
assessments.rationale: The behavior is clear and counterexamples are discoverable in public media and literature. Those resources cannot estimate drinking frequency consistently across all birds of prey.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify lung architecture, pulmonary vascularity and water intake across reptiles and other oviparous vertebrates, then test their association. Anatomical counterexamples refute universality; consistently low vascularity and intake support it.

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: comparative terrestrial-animal physiology and source references

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public comparative anatomical imaging

obstacles: Spongy and scantily supplied with blood require quantitative definitions.
Water-intake data are not broadly harmonized.
assessments.rationale: Comparative anatomy can test the lung assertion and likely expose exceptions, but no single dataset joins lung vascularity and drinking across the stated scope. Substantial literature synthesis is required.

assessments.operationalization: Compare grass-eating episodes in carnivorous mammals with independently measured illness and subsequent vomiting. Exclusive occurrence during illness and increased vomiting would support the claim; healthy grazing or no emetic association would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: plant-consumption interactions for carnivorous mammals

obstacles: Illness state is rarely recorded with feeding observations.
The purpose 'to purge' is confounded with many alternative explanations.
assessments.rationale: Plant eating and vomiting are observable, but linked longitudinal records are uncommon. Existing observations can refute 'never' in healthy animals, while the proposed function is only weakly distinguishable from alternatives.

assessments.operationalization: Use paired live and dressed-carcass weights from slaughter records to estimate dressing percentage and compare it with five-sixths, while separately testing growth rate against other livestock. Confidence intervals excluding 83.3% refute the carcass fraction.

candidate_datasets.name: FAOSTAT
candidate_datasets.role: comparative livestock production and carcass-weight statistics

obstacles: Flesh may mean a different carcass definition from modern dressed weight.
Breed and dressing practice affect yield.
assessments.rationale: Live weight, carcass weight and growth are standard livestock measurements with abundant public statistics and studies. Definition differences limit exact historical equivalence but not a strong present-day test.

assessments.operationalization: Compile verified ages at death for Camelus species and estimate typical and maximum longevity. A central lifespan near thirty supports the first clause; authenticated centenarians are required for the second.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: curated maximum-longevity records for camels

obstacles: Exceptional ages may be based on unverified husbandry reports.
Typical lifespan varies between wild and captive animals.
assessments.rationale: Longevity is directly measurable and curated records exist. The ordinary-lifespan clause is readily testable, while the claimed hundred-year extreme needs unusually strong provenance.

assessments.operationalization: Define rotten substrates chemically or by decomposition stage and compare acceptance by honey bees and diverse insect species. Any bee feeding on rotten material or another insect invariably avoiding it refutes uniqueness.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: public insect feeding-interaction records

obstacles: Rotten and sweet juice are poorly standardized.
Universal coverage across insects is impossible with current behavior data.
assessments.rationale: Targeted public studies can test honey-bee responses and find insect counterexamples. Existing data are far too sparse and heterogeneous to establish a unique invariant across insects.

assessments.operationalization: Analyze geolocated, time-stamped common-crane tracks to identify breeding and wintering endpoints and migration corridors. Tracks from northern Eurasia to Nile headwaters support the route; consistently different winter destinations refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open animal tracking datasets for migration routes

obstacles: Scythia and the ancient conception of the Nile source need geographic interpretation.
assessments.rationale: Modern tracking and occurrence data directly resolve crane routes. Historical place-name uncertainty remains, but several plausible mappings can be tested quickly.

assessments.operationalization: Compare body mass or fat score of identified migrants immediately before cold-to-warm and warm-to-cold journeys, controlling species and age. A positive within-species seasonal contrast supports the claim; reversals refute universality.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: migration timing and trajectories that can be linked to body-condition studies

obstacles: Tracking archives rarely include repeated fat measurements.
The claim ranges over all migratory animals.
assessments.rationale: Bird-banding and telemetry studies provide many partial tests, especially for quail and birds generally. Harmonized paired condition data do not cover anything close to all migrant taxa.

assessments.operationalization: Define hooked-clawed birds, measure neck proportions and tongue shape from specimens, and code vocal imitation from recordings and reports. Trait distributions and counterexamples test each generalization.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public anatomical scans for comparative morphology

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: bird vocal recordings and media

obstacles: The group oddly combines parrots with raptors.
Disposition to mimic lacks a standard species-level measure.
assessments.rationale: Morphology and vocal behavior are observable in extensive public collections, but the grouping and qualitative terms require interpretation. The component claims are testable for sampled taxa, not exhaustively.

assessments.operationalization: Under each plausible modern identification of trichia, compare occurrence and genetic records among the Black Sea, Danube and Adriatic and test whether a continuous river route exists. Geographic impossibility or absence from the Danube refutes the proposed route.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomy, distribution and migration information

obstacles: The ancient fish name is uncertain.
The claimed Danube bifurcation to the Adriatic does not exist in modern geography.
assessments.rationale: Modern distributions and hydrology can strongly assess the route, but taxonomic uncertainty prevents one definitive biological test. The mechanism is nevertheless highly discriminable under each candidate identification.

assessments.operationalization: Code seasonal inactivity in the named molluscs and relate onset to local temperature extremes, comparing hot- and cold-season dormancy. Repeatable concealment during both extremes supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: OBIS
candidate_datasets.role: time-stamped marine occurrence data for murex and scallops

obstacles: Failure to observe can mean dormancy or sampling bias.
All shellfish is much broader than available activity data.
assessments.rationale: Temperature-linked dormancy is measurable and documented in many taxa. Occurrence records are indirect and trait coverage is insufficient for the universal shellfish clause.

assessments.operationalization: For each named reptile, estimate winter inactivity duration and feeding from telemetry, activity and gut-temperature records. Four months without intake supports the claim; winter activity or feeding refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open telemetry data for reptile activity and seasonal dormancy

obstacles: Winter behavior varies greatly by latitude and climate.
Feeding cannot usually be inferred from occurrence data.
assessments.rationale: The duration and fasting prediction are explicit, but existing telemetry is patchy across the listed groups. Public data can test selected populations and readily find counterexamples.

assessments.operationalization: Use winter occurrence, banding and tracking records to determine whether each named species remains locally hidden or migrates. Winter movements and detections distinguish migration from local torpor or concealment.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: individual bird migration tracks

obstacles: Ancient vernacular names require species mapping.
A few local torpor observations do not establish species-wide strategy.
assessments.rationale: Modern occurrence and tracking coverage is excellent for these conspicuous birds. The stated alternatives are sharply discriminable, although hiding itself is harder to observe than migration.

assessments.operationalization: Compile denning, birth, den-emergence and feeding dates for female brown bears. Winter births, spring emergence near three months after solstice, and lack of food intake during denning each give direct criteria.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open brown-bear tracking and denning records

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: brown-bear life-history references

obstacles: Dates vary by latitude and reproductive status.
Metabolic fasting is not directly measured by location alone.
assessments.rationale: Brown-bear reproductive and denning biology is extensively observed and telemetry provides direct timing. Existing data can resolve all main clauses for multiple populations.

assessments.operationalization: Compile longitudinal molt observations for crabs, crayfish and lobsters and count exoskeleton shedding over individuals' lives. More than one molt directly confirms repetition.
assessments.rationale: Molting is a standard, repeatedly measured crustacean life-history process. Public databases and aquaculture studies provide decisive evidence with minimal analysis.

assessments.operationalization: Define epidemics by population-level transmission and mortality, then compile outbreaks in marine fishes. Any documented contagious mass outbreak refutes the no-epidemic assertion.

candidate_datasets.name: World Animal Health Information System
candidate_datasets.role: public reports of listed aquatic-animal disease outbreaks

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish disease information and source literature

obstacles: Surveillance strongly favors farmed and commercially important fishes.
Ancient 'pestilential' is broader than modern reportable disease.
assessments.rationale: Public outbreak records can decisively refute the universal absence claim. They do not uniformly cover wild sea fishes, but a single authenticated epidemic is sufficient for the strongest clause.

assessments.operationalization: Expose identified Bolinus brandaris and Hexaplex trunculus to controlled salinities corresponding to river mouths and measure 24-hour survival. Survival after freshwater exposure refutes the claim.
obstacles: Open data on 24-hour salinity mortality for these exact species are not known.
Tasting fresh water does not specify dose or salinity.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is experimentally crisp, but distribution data cannot substitute for acute tolerance measurements. Existing literature may constrain salinity tolerance, yet a decisive test likely needs new experiments.

assessments.operationalization: Map 'measles' to muscular cysticercosis, compare host records across species, and stratify pig cases by suckling status or age. Non-pig hosts or infected suckling piglets refute the respective clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: host-parasite interaction records

candidate_datasets.name: World Animal Health Information System
candidate_datasets.role: animal disease occurrence reports

obstacles: The historical diagnosis could include lesions other than Taenia solium cysts.
Age-at-infection data are less complete than host records.
assessments.rationale: The supplied diagnostic mapping makes the host claim directly searchable in public parasitology data. The suckling-age clause is less well covered but can be assessed from veterinary records and studies.

assessments.operationalization: Compare rabies infection and fatality after confirmed rabid-dog bites across mammal species, including humans. Human rabies cases and bitten animals that do not develop disease test the universal clauses directly.

candidate_datasets.name: World Animal Health Information System
candidate_datasets.role: public animal rabies outbreak and species reports

candidate_datasets.name: WHO Rabies data
candidate_datasets.role: public human rabies surveillance data

obstacles: Post-exposure prophylaxis changes modern human outcomes.
assessments.rationale: Rabies transmission and mortality are standardized surveillance outcomes with extensive public data. The exception for humans is directly testable and decisively resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Compare donkey, horse and mule cold-tolerance indicators and map verified donkey occurrences against winter climate in the Black Sea and Scythian regions. Presence under extreme cold refutes the distributional and tolerance generalization.

candidate_datasets.name: FAOSTAT
candidate_datasets.role: country-level domestic-ass population data

obstacles: Domestic distribution depends strongly on human husbandry.
Least able to endure requires a chosen physiological endpoint.
assessments.rationale: Present and historical occurrence evidence readily assesses absence, and comparative physiology can test cold tolerance. Human management confounds the proposed causal explanation but does not prevent resolution of its main predictions.

assessments.operationalization: For diverse insect orders, compare survival after standardized oil application to the whole body versus head, in sun and shade. Any surviving species refutes the universal claim.
obstacles: Oil type, dose and exposure duration are unspecified.
No public experiment covers more than a tiny fraction of insect diversity.
assessments.rationale: The acute mortality prediction is simple and older pest-control studies may provide counterexamples. Existing data cannot support the universal quantifier, and a comprehensive test would require extensive new experiments.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct ancient-range occurrences for lions and leopards in the specified regions from dated specimens, fossils and historical records. European leopard records refute absolute absence; regional lion records test the stated concentration.

candidate_datasets.name: Paleobiology Database
candidate_datasets.role: public fossil occurrences for ancient-range reconstruction

obstacles: The claim concerns Aristotle's period, while many records have coarse dates.
More numerous requires comparable sampling effort.
assessments.rationale: Public occurrence and fossil databases permit a strong historical biogeographic test. Relative abundance is less secure than presence or absence because preservation and collecting vary spatially.

assessments.operationalization: Compile mammal hybrid crosses, parental body sizes, gestation lengths and fertility, then model whether similarity predicts successful breeding. Frequent success among matched pairs and failure among mismatched pairs support the proposed conditions.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: species gestation and life-history traits

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: parent-species body-mass data

obstacles: No comprehensive open registry of attempted interspecific matings exists.
Phylogenetic relatedness is a major confounder.
assessments.rationale: Trait data exist, and documented hybrids provide positive cases, but failed or unattempted pairings are poorly recorded. Similarity can be evaluated as a predictor only for a biased subset.

assessments.operationalization: Use genomic parentage and reproductive records to test wolf-dog and fox-dog crosses and the ancestry of Laconian-type hounds. Hybrid genomes support a cross; incompatible chromosome biology or dog-only ancestry refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public canid genome and sequence data

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: public canid DNA barcode records

obstacles: The historical Laconian hound population may not have surviving representatives.
assessments.rationale: Wolf-dog hybridization and canid ancestry are directly resolvable from extensive genetic data. The exact extinct or transformed dog lineage is harder, but the fox-dog biological assertion is strongly testable.

assessments.operationalization: Compare known-age fish with scale radius, annuli and quantified hardness across species. Predictive age accuracy above chance supports the claim; systematic age mismatch refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish age, growth and scale-aging references

obstacles: Modern scale aging relies mainly on annuli rather than hardness.
Accuracy varies among species and older ages.
assessments.rationale: Scale-based age estimation is a standard fisheries method with abundant validation data. The specific hardness component is less routinely digitized, but size and scale structure allow the core claim to be assessed.

assessments.operationalization: Choose pre-registered behavioral measures of risk-taking and aggression as 'spirit', estimate sex differences species by species, and compare bears and leopards with the distribution. Numerous female-lower exceptions would refute universality.
obstacles: Courage has several non-equivalent operationalizations.
Sex-specific behavioral data are taxonomically sparse.
Ecological and reproductive context strongly confound comparisons.
assessments.rationale: Some measurable proxies permit restricted tests, especially aggression or boldness within well-studied species. They cannot preserve the full ancient concept or support a generalization over all sexually reproducing animals.

assessments.operationalization: Model antagonistic interaction frequency against spatial and dietary overlap, and within species compare fighting under low versus high food availability. Positive controlled associations support both clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: open antagonistic and trophic species-interaction records

obstacles: Co-occurrence and diet overlap do not imply enmity.
Interaction records are highly biased toward conspicuous taxa.
assessments.rationale: Large public occurrence and interaction resources allow comparative tests, but causality is confounded by shared habitat, abundance and phylogeny. Experimental food-shortage evidence covers only selected species.

assessments.operationalization: Compare fear and aggression in replicated wild-animal populations under sustained unlimited versus normal food while controlling human exposure. Persistent wildness despite food abundance would refute the prediction.
obstacles: Unlimited food is an unrealized counterfactual.
Provisioning co-varies with habituation to humans.
Wild and tame require behavioral thresholds.
assessments.rationale: The prediction has observable consequences, but existing provisioning observations cannot isolate food abundance from repeated human contact and selection. A decisive general test would require new controlled longitudinal data.

assessments.operationalization: Use known-age red deer photographs and specimens to model antler points and complexity from ages one through older adulthood. The exact annual sequence and loss of age discrimination after six are direct predictions.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: dated public images of red-deer antlers

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public deer skeletal specimens and scans

obstacles: Most public images lack known individual age.
Nutrition and condition strongly affect antler form.
assessments.rationale: The morphology-age relation is explicit and deer-management studies contain known-age samples. Open, harmonized individual-level age data are incomplete, so the exact schedule is only partly resolvable from public datasets.

assessments.operationalization: Review continuous birth observations of red deer and record whether, when and how often the hind consumes the placenta before it reaches the ground. Any observed non-consumption refutes the invariant wording.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public wildlife video potentially documenting deer parturition

obstacles: Wild births are rarely observed continuously.
Publication and video selection favor unusual events.
assessments.rationale: The behavior is unambiguous and individual observations can confirm occurrence or provide counterexamples. Existing public observations are too few and biased to estimate how invariant it is.

assessments.operationalization: For dogs, link illness status, grass ingestion and subsequent vomiting in time-stamped veterinary or owner records, comparing with healthy controls. Increased grass eating before vomiting supports the stated example but not intentional treatment.
obstacles: Intentional self-treatment is not directly observable.
Public linked clinical-behavioral records are sparse.
Grass eating also occurs in healthy dogs.
assessments.rationale: The sequence in dogs is measurable from existing studies, but the functional and intentional interpretation has weak discriminating power. The broad claim about many quadrupeds has little standardized coverage.

assessments.operationalization: Identify candidate trochilus species and review georeferenced video and field observations for entry into Nile-crocodile mouths, food removal and crocodile tolerance. Authenticated repeated events support the claim; intensive observation without them weighs against it.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public bird behavior media

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: public crocodile and associated-bird observations

obstacles: The bird's modern identity is disputed.
Absence of a rare interaction is difficult to establish.
assessments.rationale: The interaction has clear visual consequences and public media can expose supporting events or misidentifications. No systematic dataset samples crocodile mouths enough to establish typicality.

assessments.operationalization: Use individually marked pigeons and genetic parentage to estimate pair-bond duration, re-pairing before partner death and extra-pair mating. Any surviving-partner re-pairing tests the strict life-pair clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open individual bird tracking datasets

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public pigeon genetic resources supporting parentage studies

obstacles: Tracking locations do not by themselves identify mating.
Wild lifetime histories are often censored by disappearance.
assessments.rationale: Pair bonds and genetic mating are standard ornithological outcomes with existing studies. Public longitudinal coverage is adequate for populations, but disappearance makes a literal lifetime statement difficult.

assessments.operationalization: Code nest architecture and flight capacity for quails, partridges and comparable ground birds. Constructed nests refute the first clause; comparative models test whether reduced flight predicts simpler nests.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public nest and breeding-behavior media

obstacles: A scraped lined hollow may qualify as a nest.
The proposed usefulness is an adaptive explanation with alternative causes.
assessments.rationale: Nest type and flight ability are well documented for the named birds, allowing direct resolution of the empirical clause. The final-cause wording has lower discriminating power but predicts a testable association.

assessments.operationalization: Review predator- or human-approach observations of nesting partridges and quails for injury-feigning, displacement direction, chick escape and reunion calls. Repeated complete sequences support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public bird behavior video and audio

obstacles: The full sequence is rarely captured.
Observer-triggered records may be biased and ethically constrained.
assessments.rationale: Distraction displays are standard observable behavior and substantial public media and literature exist. Completeness and frequency across the stated taxa remain only partly represented.

assessments.operationalization: Classify web-footed species and calculate their occurrence distances from marine and inland waters. Repeated populations far from water refute the universal association.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: fine-scale habitat use by tracked waterbirds

obstacles: Near requires a pre-specified distance threshold.
assessments.rationale: Foot morphology, taxonomy and habitat occurrence are richly documented in public data. A spatial analysis can test the universal claim globally within weeks.

assessments.operationalization: Collect age, health, time-to-death, location and vocalization rates from individually monitored swans, testing whether song increases near death and whether birds move offshore. Existing recordings lacking life outcome cannot decide the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public swan vocal recordings and observation metadata

obstacles: Public recordings are not linked to subsequent death.
Musical and mournful are subjective.
Rare terminal events create severe selection bias.
assessments.rationale: The mortality-linked prediction is measurable, but available sound archives do not follow individuals to death. A decisive analysis needs new longitudinal monitoring despite abundant ordinary swan recordings.

assessments.operationalization: Compile monitored common-cuckoo nesting attempts, clutch size, incubation and host care. Any self-built nest, multi-egg laying event or maternal incubation refutes the corresponding universal clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public cuckoo and host nesting media

obstacles: One female's eggs across several host nests must not be mistaken for a clutch in one nest.
assessments.rationale: Brood parasitism is exceptionally well studied and the behavioral variables are direct. Public observations and published datasets can resolve each clause with high power.

assessments.operationalization: Boldness and nest-defense could be measured, but no observation distinguishes conscious cowardice as the purpose of brood parasitism from evolutionary and ecological alternatives.
obstacles: Conscious awareness of cowardice is inaccessible.
The final-cause explanation makes no unique observable prediction.
assessments.rationale: Cuckoo defense behavior can be compared with other birds, but that proxy does not resolve the stated mental and purposive cause. Any outcome can be redescribed as compatible with the story, giving it little discriminating power.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate eagle pair home ranges, food requirements, juvenile dispersal and neighboring-bird density from telemetry and surveys. Larger energetic needs predicting broader territories and active exclusion supports the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open eagle movement, territory and dispersal data

obstacles: Low nearby bird density can result from habitat rather than expulsion.
Eagles comprises many species.
assessments.rationale: Home range and juvenile dispersal are well represented in telemetry data, and energetic requirements are estimable. Directly attributing all neighboring-bird absence to active exclusion is more confounded, but the mechanism has testable predictions.

assessments.operationalization: Continuously video-monitor identified sea-eagle nests before fledging and score forced sun orientation, beating, eye watering and chick mortality. Absence across adequate samples or survival of affected chicks refutes the sequence.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public sea-eagle and osprey nesting media

obstacles: Existing public media are not a systematic continuous sample.
Sea-eagle identification is ambiguous.
The claimed event may be extremely rare.
assessments.rationale: The alleged actions are visually explicit, but no known open dataset samples the critical episodes with sufficient coverage. New standardized nest-camera annotation or collection is needed.

assessments.operationalization: Use anatomical records and feeding video of Lophius to test illicial filament position, prey attraction, contact and capture while concealed. Videos showing the complete lure-to-capture sequence confirm the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: anglerfish anatomy, diet and behavior references

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public anglerfish anatomical specimens and scans

obstacles: In situ predation videos are less numerous than anatomical records.
assessments.rationale: The lure and its use are concrete, distinctive traits documented in comparative anatomy and behavior. Existing public data can resolve both structure and function.

assessments.operationalization: Measure electric-organ discharges from Torpedo rays and prey or human neuromuscular responses, linking discharge to capture events. A body-generated discharge preceding prey immobilization directly supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: electric-ray biology and referenced electrophysiology

assessments.rationale: Electrical discharge and prey stunning are directly measurable and extensively established in public scientific records. The mechanism sharply distinguishes itself from mechanical capture.

assessments.operationalization: Monitor Silurus aristotelis nests continuously, identify parent sex, and measure guarding duration and attacks on small fishes. Male guarding lasting forty to fifty days supports the full claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: species reproductive behavior and source literature

obstacles: Open continuous nest records for this endemic species are limited.
Guarding duration may vary with temperature and development.
assessments.rationale: Sex, guarding and duration are clear variables, and species accounts can test occurrence. Public data likely cover few nests, limiting the exact duration and generality.

assessments.operationalization: Classify diets and movement ranges of Mediterranean fishes, testing the near-universal carnivory assertion and whether carnivores move farther than non-carnivores. Herbivorous or omnivorous counterexamples directly refute universality.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish trophic level, diet, habitat and movement information

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open aquatic-animal tracking datasets

obstacles: Wander most requires a selected movement metric.
Diet varies by life stage.
assessments.rationale: Fish diet is comprehensively represented in FishBase and can resolve the universal statement quickly. Comparative movement data are less complete, but adequate to test the second clause for a broad subset.

assessments.operationalization: Code ink discharge in cuttlefish, octopuses and squid by context: predator threat, prey approach and background concealment. Non-threat concealment in octopus or squid refutes cuttlefish uniqueness.
obstacles: Fear is an inferred internal state.
The same event can serve both defense and concealment.
Behavioral coverage is uneven among cephalopods.
assessments.rationale: Contexts and ink release are observable, and existing videos and experiments can find counterexamples. Inferring exclusive motivation weakens discrimination, so only the contextual behavioral portion is resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify Octopus vulgaris skin color relative to adjacent substrate during prey approaches and alarm events. Reduced color distance in both contexts supports the claim.
obstacles: Camouflage includes texture and pattern as well as average color.
assessments.rationale: Dynamic camouflage is directly quantifiable from existing experimental and field imagery. The two stated contexts can be compared with standard image analysis.

assessments.operationalization: Compile hatch-to-death records for Octopus vulgaris and post-spawning changes in female feeding, activity and mass. Survival beyond one year or absence of post-spawning decline tests the respective clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: curated animal longevity records

obstacles: Wild lifespan is harder to measure than captive lifespan.
As a rule needs a chosen population proportion.
assessments.rationale: Cephalopod lifespan and post-reproductive senescence are standard life-history variables with extensive records. Existing data can resolve both the typical lifespan and female decline.

assessments.operationalization: Analyze surface video of Argonauta argo in wind, tracking web deployment, arm position and movement relative to wind and current. Wind-driven acceleration with web deployment supports sailing; submerged propulsion refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: OBIS
candidate_datasets.role: georeferenced argonaut observations

obstacles: Rare offshore surface behavior has little systematic video.
Currents confound apparent wind propulsion.
assessments.rationale: The mechanical prediction is clear and existing observations can assess arm and web use. Public data are too sparse and uncontrolled for a comprehensive hydrodynamic test.

assessments.operationalization: Use developmental and anatomical imaging to locate silk glands and spinnerets, determine whether hatchlings produce silk, and trace thread material from internal glands to body surface. Internal gland origin refutes the bark-like mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public spider anatomical specimens and scans

obstacles: Off the body could merely describe the visible exit point rather than material origin.
assessments.rationale: Spider silk anatomy and juvenile spinning are extensively documented and directly observable. Modern imaging cleanly discriminates external shedding from secretion by internal glands.

assessments.operationalization: Track individually marked honey bees for complete foraging bouts and identify each visited plant taxon by video, pollen or DNA. Any mixed-species trip refutes the absolute claim; the proportion of flower-constant trips tests its typical form.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: bee-plant visitation interaction records

obstacles: Most visitation datasets do not retain trip-level sequences.
Flower identification from mixed pollen can be imperfect.
assessments.rationale: Flower constancy is a standard measurable behavior with substantial experimental literature. Existing open interaction data lack complete trip structure, so universality is only partly resolvable without targeted raw records.

assessments.operationalization: From hive videos and colony records, quantify queen killing and royal-cell destruction relative to queen number and impending swarming. Increased destruction when no swarm occurs supports regulation, but not workers' stated fear.
obstacles: Aristotle's kings must be mapped to queens.
Fear and intent are not directly measurable.
Hive-management practices alter queen replacement.
assessments.rationale: Queen elimination and cell destruction are observable and can be related to colony fission. Existing records can test the behavioral association, while the intentional explanation remains underdetermined.

assessments.operationalization: Record sting retention, tissue avulsion and survival after honey-bee workers sting substrates of differing elasticity. Death associated with a retained barbed sting and abdominal rupture supports the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public insect anatomical imaging relevant to sting morphology

obstacles: Bees can sometimes withdraw stings from other insects and survive.
assessments.rationale: The anatomy, injury and survival outcome are directly observable and extensively documented. Existing evidence can also resolve the scope conditions under which the claim holds.

assessments.operationalization: Age-mark worker bees and record task allocation and hair wear through life. Age-related shifts toward or away from foraging, plus measured setal abrasion, directly test each clause.
obstacles: Hairiness may reflect wear rather than indoor exposure.
Colony needs can reverse normal age polyethism.
assessments.rationale: Worker age and task are standard variables in honey-bee experiments with abundant existing data. The direction stated is sharply testable, as is the proposed morphology association.

assessments.operationalization: Video-record bees departing in high versus low wind and identify any deliberately carried stones, then measure flight stability with and without ballast. Repeated high-wind flights without stones refute the generalization.
obstacles: No known public dataset records carried-object identity and wind simultaneously.
Pollen or debris could be mistaken for stones.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is unusually concrete and highly discriminable, but ordinary bee datasets do not measure it. A decisive assessment needs new high-speed field observations.

assessments.operationalization: Mark workers and queens in Vespula and Polistes colonies and estimate overwinter survival and refuges. Worker survival into spring refutes the universal worker-death clause; queen recovery underground supports overwintering.
obstacles: Polistes and Vespula differ in colony cycle.
Winter non-detection alone does not prove death.
assessments.rationale: Social-wasp colony cycles and caste survival are standard, well-studied life-history outcomes. Existing observations and experiments can resolve the main claim across the named genera.

assessments.operationalization: For identified lions involved in livestock or human attacks, compare age, dental condition and hunting performance with non-conflict lions. Enrichment of old, dentally impaired individuals supports the proposed pathway.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open lion movement data that can characterize livestock-area incursions

obstacles: Attack databases rarely include dental exams.
Habitat loss, prey depletion and opportunity confound age effects.
assessments.rationale: Attack, age and tooth condition are measurable, and some case series exist. Public linked records are incomplete and observational confounding prevents a clean universal causal conclusion.

assessments.operationalization: Analyze elephant swimming observations and respiratory anatomy, testing whether submerged animals keep the trunk tip in air and move air through it. Trunk occlusion or alternative breathing would refute the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public elephant anatomical imaging

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public wildlife video of elephant aquatic behavior

assessments.rationale: The anatomical airway and snorkeling behavior are directly visible and extensively documented. Existing images, videos and anatomy provide a decisive test.

assessments.operationalization: Follow hens before and after winning fights against cocks, measuring crowing, mounting, comb and tail morphology and spur growth, while recording age and ovarian status. Trait changes specifically following victory support the claim.
obstacles: Hormonal aging or ovarian disease can masculinize hens independently of fighting.
Public longitudinal fight-linked data are scarce.
assessments.rationale: All phenotypes are measurable, and existing poultry reports can test their occurrence. The asserted causal trigger is strongly confounded and lacks adequate public longitudinal data.

assessments.operationalization: Compare castrated and intact cocks by age at procedure for comb color, crowing, mating and male-trait development. Consistent loss or prevention after verified gonadal ablation supports the claim.
obstacles: Cauterizing the rump may not reliably castrate birds.
Historical procedure differs from modern caponization.
Open individual-level datasets are limited.
assessments.rationale: Androgen-dependent traits are explicit and many poultry experiments exist. The exact described intervention is ambiguous, so current data resolve hormonal castration better than cauterization itself.

assessments.operationalization: Compare voice pitch, androgen-dependent hair and baldness in men with documented prepubertal castration versus matched intact men. Any later hair, voice lowering or baldness refutes the corresponding absolute.
obstacles: Relevant historical cohorts are small and sensitive.
Age at castration and hormone treatment are often undocumented.
Never goes bald requires long follow-up.
assessments.rationale: The phenotypes are standard clinical variables and historical eunuch cohorts provide evidence. Public individual-level data are limited, and modern hormone treatment complicates a definitive universal test.

assessments.operationalization: Follow stags castrated before and after antler growth, recording antler initiation, size and annual casting against intact controls. Any antler growth after early castration or shedding after late castration refutes the absolutes.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public deer skeletal morphology records

obstacles: Castration timing and longitudinal antler histories are rarely open.
Antler response depends on season relative to the testosterone cycle.
assessments.rationale: The intervention and outcomes are precise, and veterinary or deer-farm studies provide partial evidence. Existing open data likely do not cover enough timing conditions for the full prediction.

assessments.operationalization: Code rumination and upper-incisor presence across mammal species and calculate their association and exceptions. Ruminants with upper incisors or non-ruminants lacking them determine the limits of the rule.

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative animal traits and source references

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public skull and dentition scans

obstacles: A few acknowledged exceptions make the exact decision threshold important.
assessments.rationale: Dentition and rumination are standard species traits with broad comparative coverage. Public anatomy and natural-history records permit a straightforward phylogenetic contingency analysis.

assessments.operationalization: Compare season-dated photographs and recordings within bird species for plumage color and song features. Repeatable within-individual or population seasonal shifts support the general claim; the blackbird example can be assessed separately.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: season-dated bird photographs, video and audio

obstacles: Age and molt can be confounded with season.
The historical owsel may not map exactly to Turdus merula.
assessments.rationale: Large public media archives contain the needed dates, colors and vocalizations. Standard image and acoustic analyses can test many species and the stated example.

assessments.operationalization: Compare morphology, genomes, banded individuals and seasonal occurrences of robin versus redstart and garden warbler versus blackcap. Distinct genomes and simultaneous populations refute seasonal transformation.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public sequence data for the four bird species

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: public DNA barcode records

obstacles: Ancient names must be mapped carefully, though the proposed modern pairs are explicit.
assessments.rationale: Species identity and seasonal presence are exceptionally well covered by genetic and occurrence data. Multiple independent analyses decisively distinguish transformation from separate migratory species.

assessments.operationalization: Code dust- and water-bathing events by species, locomotor ecology, habitat and talon morphology from public videos and species accounts. Counterexamples test each categorical association.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public bird bathing-behavior media

obstacles: Absence of bathing in media is not evidence of absence.
Crooked versus straight talons needs a morphological rule.
assessments.rationale: Positive bathing observations are plentiful and can refute universal exclusions. Systematic behavior coverage across the broad bird groups is incomplete, limiting confirmation.

assessments.operationalization: No observation can rank final cause as metaphysically prior to motor cause without first adopting Aristotle's causal framework.
obstacles: Priority among kinds of cause is a conceptual claim.
No unique measurable consequence distinguishes it from rival causal vocabularies.
assessments.rationale: This is a methodological and metaphysical ordering of explanations, not a biological prediction. Scientific datasets can describe mechanisms and functions but cannot settle the asserted ontological priority.

assessments.operationalization: Use embryological time series to determine whether vertebrae arise by patterned segmentation before fetal contortion or by fracture of a continuous backbone. Observed somitic segmentation without breakage refutes Empedocles' mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public vertebrate embryological and anatomical imaging

obstacles: The broader denial that animal characters are incidental is too sweeping, but the vertebral example is direct.
assessments.rationale: Modern embryology records the temporal origin of vertebral segmentation and sharply discriminates patterned development from accidental breakage. Existing imaging resolves the stated example directly.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate parent-offspring resemblance and genetic transmission for specified traits using pedigrees and genomes, while separating inherited from environmental effects. Heritable resemblance supports the claim; no parental predictive contribution would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public genomic sequences across animals

candidate_datasets.name: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public genotype-trait association data, especially in humans

obstacles: Certain characters is unspecified.
Parent phenotype alone does not establish a developmental mechanism.
assessments.rationale: Inheritance and parent-offspring resemblance are represented by enormous public genomic and pedigree resources. The general wording is broad, but many explicit trait operationalizations can directly test its core.

assessments.operationalization: Locomotion can be measured, but 'intellect' has no species-neutral operational definition that preserves the categorical claim; cognitive task performance tests narrower abilities only.
obstacles: Intellect is undefined and anthropocentric.
No finite behavioral battery establishes absence of intellect.
Different cognitive capacities yield conflicting classifications.
assessments.rationale: Animal cognition datasets can compare memory, planning or problem solving, but none resolve the philosophical category asserted here. The human-only boundary changes with the chosen proxy, so the claim as stated lacks a discriminating empirical criterion.

assessments.operationalization: Measure respiratory airflow, core and respiratory-tract temperature and heat exchange through breathing cycles across air-breathing animals. If airflow persists without the predicted heat alternation or is driven by pressure-generating muscles and gas demand, the stated necessary mechanism is refuted.

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open metabolic-rate measurements and source references across terrestrial animals

obstacles: Heat discharge may be an effect of ventilation rather than its driver.
Coverage is richer for mammals and birds than other air breathers.
assessments.rationale: Respiratory mechanics, temperature and metabolism are standard physiological measurements with extensive public records. Temporal and intervention evidence can distinguish thermal driving from rival muscular and chemical-control mechanisms.

assessments.operationalization: Code wings and flight behavior across ant species and castes. Verified winged flying reproductives and wingless workers within ants directly confirm that the group spans both categories.
obstacles: Flight status differs mainly by caste and life stage rather than species.
assessments.rationale: Winged reproductive ants and wingless workers are directly documented in extensive public collections. The classification point is decisively testable with standard morphology and observation.

assessments.operationalization: Map each named kind to domestic taxa and their wild conspecific, feral, or ancestral populations, then test whether every kind contains both tame and wild members. A documented kind lacking any wild population would refute the near-universal statement.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts describing domestication, behavior, and wild distributions

obstacles: Tame, wild, feral, and ancestral wild populations are not equivalent categories.
The Indian dog example is taxonomically and historically ambiguous.
assessments.rationale: The named examples and tame/wild contrast are measurable, but substantial category interpretation is required. Public occurrence and species-account data cover the examples unevenly and cannot by themselves establish behavioral tameness for individual records.

assessments.operationalization: One could compare classifications produced by multivariate clustering with successive binary splits against accepted animal phylogenies, but no empirical threshold determines which grouping mankind instinctively recognizes or which classification animals should use.
obstacles: The claim is normative about proper classification.
Natural group and instinctive recognition lack unique measurable criteria.
assessments.rationale: Phylogenetic and trait data could compare algorithms, but could not settle the stated prescription without choosing a definition of naturalness in advance. Almost any result can be accommodated by changing the selected differentiae or similarity criterion.

assessments.operationalization: Encode homologous and analogous anatomical characters for birds and fishes, then test whether within-class variation is exclusively quantitative while between-class correspondences are exclusively analogous. Any within-class qualitative absence or novel structure refutes the strict claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: ontology-linked vertebrate anatomical phenotypes and homology-relevant characters

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: comparative three-dimensional anatomy of bird and fish specimens

obstacles: Degree versus kind is partly dependent on character coding.
No database exhaustively covers soft and hard anatomy across both classes.
assessments.rationale: The universal exclusivity can be tested for many coded structures, and counterexamples would be informative. Existing resources are taxonomically and anatomically incomplete, while the analogy judgment requires specialist homology decisions.

assessments.operationalization: Across mapped animal clades, code respiratory organs, circulating fluids, and their gas-transport or nutrient-transport functions. Test whether every lungless or bloodless group has a distinct structure or fluid performing the asserted corresponding office.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: comparative anatomical phenotype records for vertebrate organs

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: reviewed accounts of respiratory and circulatory anatomy across animal groups

obstacles: Bloodless animals spans many unrelated invertebrate phyla.
Analogy and same office require functional judgments not consistently encoded.
assessments.rationale: Respiratory structures and circulating fluids are observable, but the asserted analogies are interpretive. Public comparative resources can resolve selected clades, not the full scope of all animals.

assessments.operationalization: Functions and structure-function adaptation can be measured for particular parts, but no observation distinguishes a body made for a soul from the same body produced without that final cause.
obstacles: Soul and made for are not measurable biological variables.
The final-cause explanation adds no distinguishing prediction.
assessments.rationale: Individual organ functions are empirical, but the universal teleological relation is not. Existing anatomy data would document adaptation without testing the asserted direction of purpose.

assessments.operationalization: Code tissues and organs by material composition and test whether heterogeneous organs perform the listed actions while homogeneous tissues compose them. The further assertion that tissues exist for organs has no separate observable criterion.

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon
candidate_datasets.role: cross-species anatomical partonomy linking tissues, organs, and body parts

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

assessments.operationalization: Define neck as a distinct mobile region between head and trunk and code it with lung presence across blooded animals, especially fishes. A lungless animal with such a neck or a lunged animal without one refutes the biconditional implication.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase

assessments.operationalization: Code an anatomically homologous epiglottis, lungs, and integument across mammals, birds, and reptiles. An epiglottis in a feathered or scaled animal, or its absence in a hairy lunged mammal, refutes exclusivity.

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon

Soft-tissue laryngeal anatomy is underrepresented in museum imaging.
Species-level exceptions are hard to screen exhaustively.
assessments.rationale: The co-occurring anatomical traits are measurable and public comparative sources cover major clades. Soft-tissue and homology coverage are insufficient for the universal scope.

assessments.operationalization: Define each listed viscus by structure and function, then code homologous or analogous internal organs across vertebrates and major invertebrate phyla. A bloodless animal with an organ meeting the fixed definition refutes the categorical absence.

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web

assessments.operationalization: Use staged embryo imaging and expression data to record first appearance of cardiac tissue, beating, blood cells, and other organs across vertebrates. candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN

assessments.operationalization: Compare sensory-evoked activity and causal lesion or stimulation effects in brain, peripheral nerves, and heart. Sensation-specific neural activity and loss of sensation after neural disruption despite an intact heart refute the heart-as-primary-seat mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: OpenNeuro

candidate_datasets.name: Allen Brain Map
candidate_datasets.role: public neural circuits, activity, and connectivity resources

assessments.operationalization: Measure heart centroid relative to the sagittal plane in humans and a broad vertebrate sample from imaging. candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive

The coldness explanation lacks matched side-temperature data.

assessments.operationalization: Use CT, histology, and veterinary anatomy to record ossa cordis in horses, cattle breeds, and other mammals. A normal ossified cardiac skeleton in another animal, or absence in the named taxa, refutes the exclusivity.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: comparative mammalian anatomy accounts

A certain kind of ox is unspecified.
