assessments.operationalization: Count anatomically defined heart chambers across blooded animals and model chamber number as a function of adult body size and lineage. Small animals with more chambers or large animals with fewer directly refute the asserted size rule.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: comparative vertebrate circulatory anatomy and body size

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: cardiac and whole-body anatomical imaging where available

obstacles: Atrium, ventricle, sinus venosus, and partial septa make chamber counting scheme-dependent.
Phylogeny strongly confounds size.
Soft-tissue cardiac data are not comprehensive.
assessments.rationale: Modern comparative anatomy provides many decisive size and chamber examples. The universal scope and chamber-definition differences require harmonization, but a substantial portion is resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Define relative heart mass and standardized threat-boldness behavior, then test their association across the named mammals and a broader phylogenetic sample. A null or positive association between relative heart size and courage refutes the direction.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: body size and qualitative behavior accounts for the named mammals

obstacles: Timid and courageous are not standardized across species.
Heart mass and behavioral assays are rarely available for the same individuals or taxa.
Body size, metabolism, and domestication are strong confounds.
assessments.rationale: The relationship is testable in principle, but current public data do not jointly measure comparable boldness and heart size across the required species. Qualitative natural-history labels cannot adequately discriminate the proposed relation.

assessments.operationalization: Use lineage tracing and isotopic nutrient-flow data to quantify the contribution of blood-borne cells and molecules to each tissue during development and maintenance. Tissues built from local progenitors while merely receiving nutrients would refute a literal blood-as-material reading.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: public lineage, developmental, and tissue-formation experiments

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public developmental lineage and vascular imaging

obstacles: Material could mean cellular precursor, nutrient source, or transport medium.
No dataset traces every body part across all blooded animals.
Vessel distribution alone does not establish material origin.
assessments.rationale: Modern developmental data can distinguish blood cells from transported nutrients in model organisms. Ambiguous material language and universal scope permit only partial resolution.

assessments.operationalization: Across fishes and other vertebrates, code lungs and gills and analyze respiratory heat exchange from measured water or air flow and body temperature. candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish respiratory organs, habitats, and taxonomy

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: comparative respiratory physiology and anatomy accounts

obstacles: Some fishes possess lungs or use air breathing.
Respiration and thermoregulation are coupled differently in ectotherms and endotherms.
Gills exchange gases, ions, and heat simultaneously.
assessments.rationale: Organ presence is broadly documented and yields decisive counterexamples to the categorical fish statement. Existing data test the cooling mechanism only in selected taxa and do not establish cooling as the necessary primary function.

assessments.operationalization: Measure lung volume relative to body size, vascular fraction, tissue water content, compliance, and inflation capacity across mammals, birds, reptiles, and other oviparous vertebrates. Overlap or reversed group differences refute the categorical contrast.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: comparative respiratory anatomy and whole-body imaging

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web

Viviparity occurs in multiple vertebrate lineages.
Comparable vascular and compliance data are scattered.
assessments.rationale: The anatomical and material properties are measurable, but no unified public dataset contains them across the stated reproductive groups. Existing evidence can test representative clades and individual components.

assessments.operationalization: Code homologues of heart and liver and all other defined viscera across vertebrate lineages. A blooded animal lacking either organ or another viscus present in every sampled lineage refutes the corresponding universal or uniqueness statement.

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon
candidate_datasets.role: cross-species organ definitions, homologies, and taxonomic constraints

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: comparative vertebrate internal anatomy

Universal absence is difficult to establish from incomplete coding.
assessments.rationale: Comparative anatomy and ontologies can test major vertebrate groups with clear counterexamples. Exhaustive coverage and the category of viscera limit full resolution.

assessments.operationalization: Code urinary bladder presence across birds, reptiles, and fishes, with tortoises and turtles separated, using a fixed definition that excludes transient cloacal expansion. Any nontortoise covered species with a true bladder refutes the claimed exception pattern.

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web

assessments.operationalization: Inspect renal anatomy across birds, fishes, reptiles, and tortoises, distinguishing true kidneys from kidney-like bodies by histology and excretory function. A true kidney in any non-tortoise feathered or scaled animal refutes the categorical claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon

assessments.operationalization: Measure the cranial-caudal position of paired kidneys in standardized body coordinates across species. Any typical species or individual with the left kidney higher than or level with the right refutes always.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

assessments.operationalization: Code upper and lower incisor presence and count distinct stomach chambers in viviparous blooded animals, beginning with the named taxa. Any qualifying animal with multiple true stomach chambers refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web

assessments.operationalization: One could order taxa by selected traits and quantify pairwise differences, but no data-independent definition identifies the one natural sequence, its neighbours, or how small a difference counts as unbroken.

assessments.operationalization: Use gut-content, stable-isotope, and feeding observations to estimate whether cicadas obtain sufficient nutrition from atmospheric deposits rather than xylem sap. Consistent xylem feeding or dependence on plant-derived fluid would refute the main assertion.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

candidate_datasets.role: avian ophthalmology, developmental regeneration studies, and historical replication reports

obstacles: Ethically, the stated injury cannot be newly induced merely to test the claim.
Existing records may concern superficial injury rather than complete eye destruction.
Species-specific longitudinal cases are likely rare.
assessments.rationale: The prediction and refuting outcome are unusually clear. Existing literature can test related avian retinal repair or accidental injuries, but probably contains too few precisely characterized swallow cases to resolve the claim fully.

assessments.operationalization: Choose explicit congenital-defect categories, estimate sex-specific prevalence at birth in humans, and compare corresponding sex ratios in animal congenital-anomaly records. Higher prevalence among human males but not other species would support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: CDC WONDER
candidate_datasets.role: population birth and infant mortality records stratifiable by sex and congenital conditions

candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA)
candidate_datasets.role: sex-linked and other congenital phenotypes across animal species

candidate_datasets.name: Orphadata
candidate_datasets.role: human rare congenital disorder epidemiology

obstacles: 'Defective' is broad, historically loaded, and lacks a unique modern variable.
Animal surveillance is not comparable to population-level human registries.

assessments.operationalization: Compare sex-specific fetal developmental milestones or maturity at equal gestational age, age at puberty, age at peak adult performance, and survival or biological aging. The full claim requires slower prenatal female development but earlier female puberty, prime, and aging.

candidate_datasets.name: CDC WONDER
candidate_datasets.role: sex-stratified fetal, birth, and mortality outcomes

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: sex, age, pubertal-development, anthropometric, and health measures

candidate_datasets.name: Human Mortality Database
candidate_datasets.role: sex-specific mortality schedules across populations and time

obstacles: 'Prime of life' and 'old age' admit multiple operational definitions.
Prenatal developmental speed is multidimensional rather than a single variable.
assessments.rationale: Large open human datasets resolve puberty and age-related outcomes with high precision, and fetal development can be tested with defined milestones. Interpretation is needed for 'prime' and overall developmental speed, but plausible operationalizations are testable now.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate menstruation resumption and conception rates during breastfeeding, then compare milk production before and after conception. Any menstruation or conception during lactation refutes the categorical clauses, while longitudinal milk-volume changes test the drying-up prediction.

candidate_datasets.name: National Survey of Family Growth
candidate_datasets.role: public reproductive histories, pregnancy intervals, and breastfeeding variables

candidate_datasets.name: Demographic and Health Surveys Program
candidate_datasets.role: large public survey datasets on breastfeeding, postpartum amenorrhea, and birth intervals

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: longitudinal studies of lactation during pregnancy and milk production

obstacles: Milk volume during a subsequent pregnancy is less widely measured than amenorrhea and conception.

assessments.operationalization: Code fetal presentation at natural delivery across viviparous species and test whether head-first is universal or predominant. Any species in which normal births are routinely posterior-first refutes the universal, while fetal mass distribution data can separately test the proposed explanation.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: obstetric and veterinary studies reporting fetal presentation by species

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open supplementary datasets from comparative reproductive studies

Clinical records overrepresent difficult births.
The causal weight explanation needs different anatomical data.

assessments.operationalization: Compare validated maximum longevity and adult survival across humans, elephants, and other animals. A credibly documented non-elephant species exceeding human maximum lifespan refutes the ranking.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: curated maximum longevity records across animal species

candidate_datasets.name: Human Mortality Database
candidate_datasets.role: validated human mortality and longevity data

candidate_datasets.name: COMADRE Animal Matrix Database
candidate_datasets.role: open demographic matrices and survival data for animal populations

Unequal observation effort biases species maxima.

assessments.operationalization: Fit phylogenetic models of gestation length using neonatal mass, adult mass, lifespan, placental type, and developmental state, then compare the independent predictive contribution of offspring size and lifespan. candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: gestation, body mass, offspring mass, and life-history traits

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: gestation, longevity, and body-size variables across mammals

obstacles: Comparative correlations cannot uniquely establish Aristotle's developmental mechanism.
Offspring size, adult size, developmental state, and lifespan are evolutionarily correlated.

assessments.operationalization: Compare recorded gestation ranges for Equus species, humans, and elephant species with the stated one-year, ten-month maximum, and two-year values. Species ranges containing or contradicting those values directly resolve each clause.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: curated gestation lengths for horses, asses, humans, and elephants

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: independent comparative mammalian gestation values

obstacles: Ancient months may be lunar rather than modern calendar months.
Species and individual gestation ranges must not be reduced to a single mean.
assessments.rationale: These are direct, standard life-history variables for well-studied species. Multiple open comparative databases provide sufficient coverage and the numerical assertions can be checked in days.

assessments.operationalization: No observation of eye-colour variation distinguishes absence of a final cause from an empirically identical material or efficient account unless an independent measurable definition of final causation is supplied.
obstacles: Final causation has no independent measurable criterion here.
The proposed alternatives can accommodate the same observed colour distribution.
assessments.rationale: Eye colour itself is measurable, but the claim concerns which metaphysical kind of cause applies. Without a distinct prediction for final causation, datasets cannot confirm or refute the stated distinction.

assessments.operationalization: Define fetal sleep and wake states from validated heart-rate, movement, and neurophysiological criteria, estimate time in each state, and compare with newborn sleep duration. candidate_datasets.name: PhysioNet
candidate_datasets.role: open physiological time-series collections, including fetal and neonatal recordings usable for state classification

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: fetal behavioral-state studies across humans and oviparous animals

The claimed causal link to newborn sleep is not isolated by descriptive data.
Broad animal coverage is limited.

assessments.operationalization: Code synchronized video and sleep-state recordings of newborn facial behavior for laughter-like vocalizations and crying while awake versus asleep. Any unambiguous awake laughter refutes the categorical claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Databrary
candidate_datasets.role: research video library containing developmental and infant behavior recordings

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: neonatal smiling, laughter, crying, and sleep-state studies

assessments.operationalization: Measure iris colour from calibrated longitudinal images at birth and later infancy in humans and comparable animal cohorts. candidate_datasets.name: Databrary
candidate_datasets.role: publicly discoverable longitudinal infant video suitable for coded eye-colour observations where resolution permits

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: longitudinal infant iris pigmentation studies and veterinary comparisons

obstacles: Lighting and camera white balance make retrospective colour coding unreliable.
Birth images and later follow-up are rarely linked in open datasets.
Cross-animal neonatal iris data are sparse.
assessments.rationale: The universal human assertion is easy to refute with calibrated counterexamples, but suitable open longitudinal colour data are limited. The cross-animal clause greatly exceeds current standardized coverage.

assessments.operationalization: Compile verified heterochromia records by species and quantify eye-colour diversity within species. A confirmed heterochromic individual of any nonhuman, nonhorse animal refutes the exclusivity clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA)
candidate_datasets.role: curated animal pigmentation and heterochromia phenotypes

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: public georeferenced photographs that can document heterochromia in diverse species

obstacles: Photographic artefacts and eye disease can mimic congenital heterochromia.
Absence of observations cannot rank eye-colour diversity across all animals.
assessments.rationale: The exclusivity assertion has decisive, photographically verifiable counterexamples and public phenotype resources. The superlative claim that horses have the greatest variety would require a systematic animal-wide sampling design not present in current data.

assessments.operationalization: Compare standardized photopic and scotopic visual-acuity or contrast-sensitivity tests among people grouped by measured iris pigmentation, controlling age, refractive error, ancestry, and ocular disease. candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: public visual-acuity, ophthalmic, demographic, and health measurements for human participants

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: studies and supplements linking iris pigmentation with glare, acuity, and dark adaptation

obstacles: Large population datasets may lack both iris colour and scotopic testing.
Ancestry and ocular pigmentation covary with several visual and environmental factors.
assessments.rationale: The hypothesis maps to standard vision tests, but no single named open cohort clearly contains iris colour plus matched day and night performance. Existing studies permit partial tests with meaningful confound control.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate cataract and clinically defined night-blindness prevalence by iris pigmentation, controlling age, ancestry, UV exposure, diabetes, and inherited retinal disease. Opposing excess risks in light- and dark-eyed groups would support the two-part claim.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: population ophthalmic examinations, visual function, and relevant health covariates

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public association summaries for iris pigmentation and ocular-disease phenotypes

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: epidemiological studies of iris pigmentation, cataract, and night blindness

obstacles: Nyctalopia is a symptom with heterogeneous causes.
Iris colour is strongly associated with ancestry and UV exposure.
Open cohorts may not contain all variables jointly.
assessments.rationale: Both outcomes have modern clinical definitions and substantial public ophthalmic data. Joint individual-level data on pigmentation and both diagnoses are incomplete, and confounding limits causal interpretation.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify eye prominence or orbital depth from specimens and pair it with species-level distance acuity measured under comparable conditions. A negative association between prominence and long-distance acuity after controlling eye size and ecology would support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public 3D specimen media for quantifying orbit and eye placement

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts for ecology and sensory adaptations

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: species-specific visual-acuity measurements

Comparable behavioral acuity data exist for relatively few species.
Eye size, retinal anatomy, and ecology are major confounders.

assessments.operationalization: Inspect anatomical descriptions and specimen images for external pinnae versus external auditory openings in Phocidae. Consistent absence of pinnae with patent ear canals supports the anatomical claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public specimen images and 3D anatomical media for seals

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public taxon accounts describing phocid external anatomy

obstacles: The ecological 'because' clause is harder to identify causally than the anatomy.

assessments.operationalization: Code age-associated loss of hair or coat pigmentation from longitudinal or age-known individuals across mammals, including humans and horses. Clear visible greying in another species refutes the near-exclusive assertion.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: public animal photographs potentially documenting age-associated coat greying

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: species aging context and longevity for comparative sampling

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: veterinary and comparative reports of age-related depigmentation

Seasonal coat change and individual markings can mimic greying.
Animal-wide absence cannot be established from opportunistic records.

assessments.operationalization: Use longitudinal scalp photographs or clinical records to map the first region of patterned hair loss and first region of greying in men. Temporal or clinical evidence of temporal or occipital balding onset would refute the universal negative.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: clinical studies and supplements on male-pattern alopecia and spatial patterns of canities

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public phenotype association records for male-pattern baldness and hair greying

Alopecia subtypes other than androgenetic alopecia complicate 'no one'.

assessments.operationalization: Measure hair curvature in geographically sampled populations and model it against long-term local temperature and humidity while controlling ancestry. candidate_datasets.name: WorldClim
candidate_datasets.role: open historical temperature and precipitation layers for population locations

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public association summaries for hair morphology traits

assessments.operationalization: Link sea-urchin specimens with collection depth and temperature, measure test size and spine length or hardness, and model trait differences across depth within species. Small bodies with disproportionately large, hard spines in cold deep water support the pattern.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media for test and spine morphometrics

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS)

assessments.operationalization: Estimate clinically defined scalp hair-loss prevalence and pattern in women, intact men, and castrated or androgen-deprived men. Documented female or eunuch baldness refutes the categorical claim; group differences test its weaker empirical implication.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: population health and examination data for sex-stratified hair-loss analyses where available

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public genetic association records for alopecia phenotypes

assessments.operationalization: Search taxonomically verified observations and specimen records for wholly or extensively white individuals of partridges, ravens, sparrows, and bears, excluding normally white species, seasonal coats, and photographic artefacts. candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist

candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA)

assessments.operationalization: Measure drinking-water temperature and longitudinal hair pigmentation in genetically and environmentally comparable cattle or goats. candidate_datasets.name: PubMed

assessments.operationalization: For animals with patterned coloration, compare calibrated ventral-belly luminance with dorsal and lateral homologous regions from standardized images. Any reliably darker underside supplies a counterexample to the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: large public image collection spanning many patterned animal species

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media with multiple anatomical views

assessments.operationalization: Estimate fundamental frequency from sex-identified adult vocal recordings within species, then compare female-minus-male pitch across taxa and specifically in cattle. Higher female pitch generally and lower cow pitch would support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: publicly accessible animal sound archive with taxonomic metadata

candidate_datasets.name: Xeno-canto
candidate_datasets.role: open wildlife sound recordings, especially birds

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad

assessments.operationalization: Inspect bovine cardiac anatomy records, necropsies, and images for an os cordis and verify mineralized structures histologically or radiographically. Any confirmed occurrence in a bull supports the existential claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: animal vocal recordings potentially including managed or altered individuals

candidate_datasets.role: human and veterinary castration studies reporting voice and behavior

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web

assessments.operationalization: No finite observation distinguishes a world in which nature never acts in vain 'so far as possible' from one containing failures, because any apparent counterexample can be redescribed as constrained possibility.
obstacles: 'In vain' and 'so far as possible' lack independent measurement criteria.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate the age distribution of third-molar gingival eruption from population dental examinations and identify verified late-life eruptions. A central eruption age near twenty plus rare substantially later cases supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: public age-linked dental examination and tooth-status data

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Specimen media for bone, hoof, feather, and scale structure in the named groups.

obstacles: Gregarious can mean a feeding flock, a roost, or a breeding colony.
Crooked talons are inferred from raptorial orders, which also include species with weaker feet.
assessments.rationale: eBird records the count variable directly, and diet tables can restrict the test to birds of prey. The morphological phrase and the social word both need a threshold the text does not give, so the analysis tests a stated proxy rather than a single coded trait. Within that proxy, large vulture or falcon counts would be enough to reject a universal ban on flocks.

assessments.operationalization: For each domesticated form in DAD-IS, ask whether IUCN and occurrence-backed taxonomies still list a wild counterpart of the same lineage; a domesticated kind with no wild counterpart, living or historically attested, would refute the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: FAO DAD-IS
candidate_datasets.role: Inventory of domesticated breeds, including horse, cattle, pig, sheep, goat, and dog.

candidate_datasets.name: IUCN Red List
candidate_datasets.role: Extinction and wild-status assessments for the proposed wild progenitors.

candidate_datasets.name: ASM Mammal Diversity Database
candidate_datasets.role: Current species list for wild and domestic mammals, used to keep the name matching explicit.

obstacles: The same kind is ambiguous once domesticates are ranked as separate species.
Several wild progenitors are extinct, so a present-day survey does not match the claim's timeframe one for one.
assessments.rationale: Breed inventories and extinction assessments cover the named livestock and many other domesticates. What they do not settle by themselves is whether aurochs and cattle, or wolf and dog, are the same kind, which is the decision the sentence requires. The named examples can be checked; the universal depends on that taxonomic choice and on extinct populations that are not in living-occurrence tables.

assessments.operationalization: Code urinary bladder and intestine as present or absent across animals that have a gut or an excretory organ; any species with a urinary bladder and no intestine would refute the implication, and species with an intestine and no bladder would confirm the 'not conversely' clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: Presence and absence of excretory and digestive structures curated from the comparative literature.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Species accounts stating whether a urinary bladder and an intestine are present, including birds and fishes.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: Zebrafish anatomy for intestine and renal structures, keeping the swim bladder separate from a urinary bladder.

obstacles: Bladder presence is not a column in the main life-history tables and has to be compiled.
A swim bladder or other air space can be mistaken for a urinary bladder.
assessments.rationale: The implication is a clean presence-absence contrast, and birds are an obvious intestine-without-bladder case already written into species accounts. Coverage across all animals with excretory organs is incomplete in the curated anatomy sources, so the test is solid for vertebrates and thin outside them. A full survey would be a literature compilation rather than a query of one trait matrix.

assessments.operationalization: For each phylum, score mechanoreception, vision, hearing, and chemoreception as present or absent; the claim holds if every animal lineage with any sense has mechanoreception and at least one lineage lacks each other sense.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Sensory descriptions for representative animals across phyla, including eyeless and earless species.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: Zebrafish sensory anatomy as a worked vertebrate case with touch, vision, hearing, and smell.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: A phylum-level tree so that gaps in sensory coverage can be counted rather than ignored.

obstacles: Touch is difficult to score in animals without neurons, especially sponges.
No public dataset inventories every sensory modality for every phylum.
assessments.rationale: Model-animal anatomy and species accounts can show that vision, hearing, and smell fail to be universal and that mechanoreception is widespread in animals with nervous systems. They do not contain a modality matrix for the whole animal kingdom, and sponges make the word sense itself unstable. The claim is testable on the groups with described sense organs and open at the base of the tree.

assessments.operationalization: Map blooded to vertebrates and bloodless to invertebrates, then compare walking-leg number; a vertebrate species with more than four legs would refute the claim, and invertebrates restricted to zero, two, or four legs would weaken the grouping.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Body-plan accounts giving leg number and circulatory type for arthropods and vertebrates.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: Vertebrate versus invertebrate placement for the species being counted.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: Leg-bearing marine invertebrates, including crustaceans, with body-size and taxonomic context.

obstacles: Bloodless has to be mapped to the absence of vertebrate blood, and some invertebrates have haemoglobin.
Leg number is not a single open column across phyla.
assessments.rationale: Leg number and the vertebrate circulatory plan are standard facts in species accounts, so the main pattern can be checked without new collecting. The Aristotle word does not match a single laboratory variable, because haemoglobin and leg-like appendages occur outside the intended groups. The result is a partial test of a mapped version of the sentence, not a direct query.

assessments.operationalization: In staged embryo series, mark whether the embryo arises from a restricted germ region while the rest of the egg is yolk consumed later, and contrast that with insect larvae that reorganize the whole body; a yolk-free embryo using the entire egg as germ, or a grub leaving most of its body unused, would challenge the contrast.

candidate_datasets.name: The Virtual Human Embryo
candidate_datasets.role: Human and comparative early-embryo stages showing the germ disc separate from nutritional reserves.

candidate_datasets.name: GEISHA
candidate_datasets.role: Chicken developmental anatomy, the clearest public series for an embryo sitting on a large yolk.

obstacles: Public staging atlases cover chick, frog, and human, not every oviparous group.
The grub side of the contrast needs an insect series that these vertebrate atlases do not contain.
assessments.rationale: Chick and frog atlases show the spatial split between embryo and yolk directly, which is the measurable content of the egg half of the claim. Insect metamorphosis, the grub half, is not in those atlases and would have to be added from separate developmental collections. The vertebrate egg can be examined now; the full contrast cannot.

assessments.operationalization: Use reproductive mode to split viviparous sharks into internal egg-hatchers and placental live-bearers, and contrast both with horse and human pregnancy; absence of any internally hatching shark, or internally hatching mammals coded like those sharks, would refute the contrast.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: Reproductive guild for sharks and rays, including oviparity, yolk-sac viviparity, and placental viviparity.

candidate_datasets.name: Sharkipedia
candidate_datasets.role: Life-history traits for sharks and rays with reproductive mode as a coded field.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Accounts of human and horse pregnancy as the live-foetus side of the contrast.

obstacles: The shark kind mixes egg-laying, yolk-sac, and placental species.
Internal hatching has to be read from reproductive guild, not from a single column named eggs.
assessments.rationale: FishBase and Sharkipedia code the reproductive modes the sentence distinguishes, for most living sharks rather than a handful of case reports. Mammals in the contrast are the standard live-bearing pattern in species accounts. A table join of those fields can confirm or reject the grouping with ordinary cross-tabulation.

assessments.operationalization: Compare maximum body length of invertebrate species by habitat (marine, freshwater, terrestrial) and by climate zone of their occurrences; marine or mild-climate lineages no larger than their land and freshwater relatives would refute the two comparisons.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: Maximum length and habitat for marine and freshwater invertebrates.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Georeferenced records used to place those species in warmer or colder climates.

candidate_datasets.name: Copernicus Climate Data Store
candidate_datasets.role: Gridded air temperature used to mark mild versus cold climates for the occurrence coordinates.

obstacles: Bloodless is a wide, non-monophyletic bucket.
Published maximum lengths over-represent large or commercially noticed species.
Mild climate needs a temperature cutoff the text does not give.
assessments.rationale: Length, habitat, and climate grids exist and can be joined for a subset of invertebrates, especially marine ones. Sampling favors big, named species, and terrestrial invertebrates are less consistently measured than marine ones. The comparisons are feasible as a biased subset test, not as a balanced survey of every bloodless group.

assessments.operationalization: Code hair, including spines, and reproductive mode for living mammals; any hairy egg-layer refutes the universal, and no such species among hairy animals would support it.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Species accounts that state both the coat and whether the animal lays eggs or bears live young, including monotremes and spiny mammals.

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote life-history database
candidate_datasets.role: Life-history table for mammals with reproductive traits that separate egg-laying monotremes from viviparous mammals.

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: Mammal trait table including the monotremes and the viviparous orders, for body plan and reproduction together.

obstacles: Spines of hedgehogs and porcupines have to be counted as hair, which the claim itself allows.
Extinct hairy egg-layers, if any, are outside the living-trait tables.
assessments.rationale: Hair and egg-laying versus live birth are recorded for the living mammals these databases cover, including the monotremes that decide a universal. The scope is essentially the modern mammal list, which PanTHERIA, the amniote life-history table, and species accounts share. A small team can cross-tabulate coat and parity without new anatomical work.

assessments.operationalization: On sexed human crania, count suture lines and whether three meet at one point or a single circular suture dominates; a large overlap between male and female patterns would refute the sex rule.

candidate_datasets.name: Visible Human Project
candidate_datasets.role: Male and female cadaveric heads on which the cranial sutures can be inspected directly.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public head CT collections from which suture patterns can be read in a larger adult sample.

obstacles: Suture pattern is rarely a field in open osteometric downloads.
Series large enough for a sex comparison often remain in museum collections rather than one public table.
assessments.rationale: The variables are visible on cranial CT and on the Visible Human heads, so the criterion is concrete. Those public images are a small or clinical sample, not a sex-stratified osteological series built for this question. The pattern can be scored for the available scans; a population estimate of the sex rule would take further compilation.

assessments.operationalization: For Mediterranean Talpa and for Spalax, score external eye visibility and whether a pigmented eye remnant lies under the skin, then survey other live-bearing mammals for the same condition; an externally visible functional eye would refute the description, and a second viviparous eyeless lineage would refute the 'only' clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Eye and life-history accounts for moles and blind mole-rats.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: MicroCT and photographs of mole and mole-rat heads showing the orbital region.

candidate_datasets.name: DigiMorph
candidate_datasets.role: Digital morphology of small-mammal skulls as a complement to the eye soft tissues.

obstacles: The animal may be a Talpa mole or a Spalax mole-rat, and their eyes are not the same.
The claim that it is the only viviparous animal without eyes needs a survey beyond one genus.
assessments.rationale: Skull imaging and species accounts can test whether a pigmented eye sits under skin in both candidate taxa. They do not remove the name ambiguity, and a different mapping changes how strong the 'cannot see' and 'only' clauses are. The anatomical description is partly testable now; the uniqueness clause needs a wider mammal survey than one genus provides.

assessments.operationalization: Compare within-species iris-color variety in humans with other mammals, counting horses separately; several non-human species with stable within-species color polymorphisms would refute 'only or nearly only'.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Photographs in which iris color can be scored for humans, horses, dogs, cats, and other mammals.

candidate_datasets.name: FAO DAD-IS
candidate_datasets.role: Breed standards that record blue or odd eyes in horses, dogs, and other domesticates.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Species accounts that mention eye color when it is unusual.

obstacles: Iris color is not a column in the mammal trait databases.
'Nearly the only' has no numeric cutoff.
Photographs confound lighting, breed bias, and age.
assessments.rationale: Breed standards and photographs can show that eye-color variation is not confined to humans, which is enough to pressure the uniqueness claim. There is no curated iris-color matrix, and 'nearly only' can be saved or rejected by moving the threshold. The data support a partial, photo-based test rather than a clean comparative analysis.

assessments.operationalization: On head imaging, trace air-filled or patent ducts from the ear cavity: a duct to the nasopharynx supports the palate connection, and an open passage into the cranial cavity would refute the denial of a brain connection.

candidate_datasets.name: Visible Human Project
candidate_datasets.role: Sectioned human heads on which the ear cavity, Eustachian tube, and cranial floor can be followed.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Head CT series showing the temporal bone and nasopharynx in many adults.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Protein Atlas
candidate_datasets.role: Histology of the ear and adjacent tissues as a check on what is a passage rather than a nerve.

obstacles: Passage can mean an air duct or any canal, and those readings disagree.
Imaging coverage is strong for humans and weak for other eared animals.
assessments.rationale: Human CT and the Visible Human sections show the middle-ear route toward the nasopharynx and the absence of an air passage into the brain. The same images include nerve canals toward the cranial cavity, so the result depends on whether those count as passages. Other mammals with ears are not in these human collections, so the scope 'animals with ears' is only partly covered.

assessments.operationalization: Score voluntary pinna movement as present or absent for humans and for other mammals that have external ears; any non-human species that cannot move its pinnae, or a human pattern of reliable movement, would refute the uniqueness claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Behavioral notes on the external ear for mammals that have pinnae.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Photographs and short observations that sometimes show ear posture changing, as a weak supplement to the accounts.

obstacles: Voluntary ear movement is not a field in trait databases.
Some humans can move the pinna, so the human side is already variable.
assessments.rationale: Species accounts occasionally mention mobile ears, but they do not score the ability across mammals, and photo archives were not built for that trait. The comparison is well defined and still lacks a dataset that records it. A test would compile natural-history notes rather than analyze a table, and even then human variation blurs the species-level contrast.

assessments.operationalization: For the Nile crocodile and for other jawed vertebrates, score whether the upper jaw, the lower jaw, or both move relative to the braincase during a bite; movement of the crocodile's lower jaw, or upper-jaw movement in another lineage, would refute the two clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Skull models showing the jaw joint and cranial joints of crocodiles, birds, and other vertebrates.

candidate_datasets.name: DigiMorph
candidate_datasets.role: Additional skull reconstructions for the same comparison of joint structure.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Species accounts of how the crocodile jaw and bird or mammal jaws are described as moving.

obstacles: Joint shape does not by itself show which element moves in a living bite.
Kinematic comparisons for birds and fishes are mostly in papers rather than one movement archive.
assessments.rationale: Skeletal repositories make the joints inspectable, and species accounts state the familiar crocodile story. Movement is a behavioral variable, and bone shape underdetermines it, especially where birds and some fishes also have mobile upper jaws. Existing skeletal data can frame the test; a decisive kinematic comparison still has to be compiled from scattered studies.

assessments.operationalization: Count rib pairs on human torso CTs and on the Visible Human sections; a typical count of eight pairs would support the claim, and a typical count far from eight would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: TotalSegmentator CT dataset
candidate_datasets.role: Segmented human torso CTs in which the ribs are labeled and can be counted.

candidate_datasets.name: Visible Human Project
candidate_datasets.role: Cadaveric sections of the human trunk used as a direct rib count.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Further public chest CT collections for the same count in more adults.

obstacles: Cervical or lumbar ribs occur as uncommon variants, so the test needs a stated typical range.
Clinical CT collections over-represent patients.
assessments.rationale: Rib number is a direct anatomical count, and more than one public CT resource labels or displays the human ribcage. The claim is about humans, which is the population those collections sample. A small team can tally pairs and compare the distribution with eight without gathering new scans.

assessments.operationalization: Rank brain mass divided by body mass, and separately brain water fraction, across vertebrates; humans outside the top rank on either measure would refute that half of the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Comparative Mammalian Brain Collections
candidate_datasets.role: Brain and body weights for a wide range of mammals, used for a relative-size ranking.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: Body mass and longevity context for the same species when a weight is missing from the brain collection.

obstacles: Moistness is not in the comparative brain-size tables.
Relative size can mean a simple ratio or an encephalization residual, and those rank species differently.
assessments.rationale: Public brain-and-body weights can test whether humans have the largest brain for their size, under an explicit size correction. Water content of brain tissue is not part of those collections, so the moistest half of the sentence has no matching open table. The size clause is a real comparative test; the moisture clause is not, on current deposits.

assessments.operationalization: Score brain tissue for blood, for vessels inside it, and for temperature relative to the body surface; vessels or blood in the tissue refute the first two clauses, and a brain as warm as the body core would refute cold to the touch.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Protein Atlas
candidate_datasets.role: Human brain histology, including vascular markers, as a direct check on blood and vessels in the tissue.

candidate_datasets.name: Visible Human Project
candidate_datasets.role: Gross sections of the human head showing vessels associated with the brain.

candidate_datasets.name: Comparative Mammalian Brain Collections
candidate_datasets.role: Comparative mammal brain sections showing whether a vascular pattern is visible beyond humans.

obstacles: Cold to the touch is not in the anatomical atlases.
Vessels in the meninges have to be separated from vessels inside the brain if the claim is read narrowly.
assessments.rationale: Histology and gross anatomy can refute a bloodless, veinless brain in humans and in other mammals represented in the brain collections. Temperature is a third clause and is not in those image sets. Because the sentence is a conjunction, vascular data test part of it cleanly and leave the thermal part open.

assessments.operationalization: Count heart cavities and rank them by volume on the right, left, and middle; three cavities with the right largest and the left smallest would support the claim, and a stable count of four, or a different size order, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Visible Human Project
candidate_datasets.role: Sectioned human hearts in which the chambers can be counted and compared.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Cardiac CT and MRI collections for chamber counts in more people.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Comparative notes on the hearts of other large mammals named in the same discussion, such as the horse.

obstacles: The three cavities may not line up one for one with modern atria and ventricles.
Soft-tissue series are dense for humans and thinner for other large blooded animals.
assessments.rationale: Chamber number and relative size are visible in public human heart imaging, and the claim includes man among the animals it describes. A mismatch with three cavities, or with the stated size order, decides the sentence for that core case. Other large mammals are less completely imaged, but they are not required to refute a general count that is supposed to hold for man as well.

assessments.operationalization: Rank organs of mammals by blood volume, perfusion, or histological vessel density and see whether the lung is first; another organ ahead of the lung on the chosen measure would refute 'most richly supplied'.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Protein Atlas
candidate_datasets.role: Histology of human lung and other organs for a vessel-density comparison.

candidate_datasets.name: HuBMAP
candidate_datasets.role: Spatial assays of human lung and neighboring organs.

candidate_datasets.name: Visible Human Project
candidate_datasets.role: Gross sections showing how extensively the lung is filled with vessels versus other viscera.

obstacles: Most richly can mean flow, volume, or vessel density, and those rankings need not match.
Quantitative perfusion data are concentrated in humans and a few model mammals.
assessments.rationale: Human atlases can compare the lung with other organs on histology and gross blood content, which is the observable content of the sentence. They do not encode one agreed richness metric, and they barely leave humans and model species. The claim is testable as a human and model-mammal proxy, not as a survey of every viviparous lung.

assessments.operationalization: Measure the craniocaudal position of the right and left kidneys; the claim is supported if the right sits higher in the animals that have kidneys, and refuted if the left is higher in a large share of that scope, including humans.

candidate_datasets.name: TotalSegmentator CT dataset
candidate_datasets.role: Human CTs with left and right kidney labels, so their relative height can be measured.

candidate_datasets.name: Visible Human Project
candidate_datasets.role: Cadaveric sections of the human abdomen for the same left-right comparison.

candidate_datasets.name: The Cancer Imaging Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Additional abdominal CT series for a larger human sample.

obstacles: The open segmentations are human, so other vertebrates are not in the same table.
Horseshoe or pelvic kidneys have to be set aside as positional anomalies.
assessments.rationale: Relative kidney height is a direct measurement on labeled abdominal CTs, and humans fall inside 'all animals that have kidneys'. A systematic human pattern with the left kidney higher would refute the universal as stated. Other species are not needed for that refutation, though they would be needed to test how far any corrected version extends.

assessments.operationalization: Count separate cervical vertebrae in lion skeletons; one single neck bone would support the claim, and a series of distinct vertebrae would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Lion skeleton scans and photographs on which the neck vertebrae can be counted.

candidate_datasets.name: DigiMorph
candidate_datasets.role: Further digital skulls and skeletons of large cats for the cervical series.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: The standard vertebral formula for the lion as a check on the specimens.

obstacles: A pathologically fused neck in one specimen would have to be separated from the species condition.
assessments.rationale: Cervical count is visible on skeletal media, and lion specimens are the sort of material these repositories hold. The decision criterion is a simple count against one bone. A few normally segmented necks decide the species-level claim without a new dissection series.

assessments.operationalization: From accelerometry or direct observation, classify elephant sleep as standing or recumbent; regular sleep while standing would refute the claim, and sleep only while lying on the side would support it.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: Elephant tracking studies, some with accelerometers that can separate recumbent from standing rest.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Behavioral summaries of elephant rest posture.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Opportunistic photographs of resting elephants as a weak supplementary source.

obstacles: Most tracking sets record location rather than lying versus standing.
Published sleep studies cover a small number of elephants.
assessments.rationale: Posture during sleep is observable, and a few elephant movement studies have the sensor types that can detect it. The public sample is a handful of animals, not the species at large, and many collars were not deployed for sleep. The claim can be checked for those studied animals and not generalized from a broad open table.

assessments.operationalization: Code living ungulates for horns (none, one pair, or more) and for cloven versus solid hooves; a solid-hoofed species with a pair of horns would refute the universal, and the horned majority can be counted directly.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Hoof and horn descriptions for cattle, deer, horses, rhinos, and other ungulates.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Foot and skull specimens showing the hoof and the horn cores.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: Published morphological matrices that code hooves and cranial appendages.

obstacles: Horn and hoof type are not columns in the main mammal life-history tables.
Rhino horns and giraffe ossicones need an explicit rule before they are counted as horns.
assessments.rationale: The combination the sentence forbids is morphologically clear, and species accounts plus skeletal matrices cover the living ungulates well enough for a compilation. Those characters are not already joined in PanTHERIA-style tables, so the work is harmonizing existing codes rather than downloading one file. Within that compilation the solid-hoof plus paired-horn cell is a sharp test.

assessments.operationalization: List horned mammals that shed and regrow the head weapon each year, and record the age at first shedding; any non-deer that sheds, or deer that do not shed after age two, would refute the corresponding clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Antler and horn accounts for deer, bovids, and the pronghorn, including whether the structure is shed.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Dated photographs of shed antlers and of animals in velvet as evidence of an annual cycle.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: Age and maturation fields used when an account gives shedding relative to age.

obstacles: Other cervids, and the pronghorn, also shed headgear, so 'the deer' has to be delimited.
Age at first shedding is mostly in husbandry notes rather than a trait column.
assessments.rationale: Shedding versus permanent horns is described for the main families in species accounts and can be checked against photographs of cast antlers. Age two as the onset is a narrower fact and is not a standard coded field. The uniqueness and annual-cycle clauses are partly testable; the age threshold is the weak part.

assessments.operationalization: For fox, wolf, marten, and weasel, score whether the penis contains a bone; a bone in each named group would support the claim, and a consistently cartilaginous penis in any of them would refute it for that animal.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Baculum specimens and scans for canids and mustelids.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Species accounts that state whether a baculum is present in these carnivores.

candidate_datasets.name: DigiMorph
candidate_datasets.role: Skeletal media for the same genera when a penile bone has been imaged with the skeleton.

obstacles: Marten and weasel each cover several species.
A bone that ossifies only in adults can be missed in a young specimen.
assessments.rationale: The scope is four named carnivore groups, and both specimen repositories and species accounts treat the baculum as an ordinary anatomical fact for them. A small team can check those taxa directly rather than compile a new survey of all mammals. Adult specimens are the right sample, which is a manageable filter.

assessments.operationalization: Code mammals for tusks, horns, and interlocking pointed cheek teeth; any species with both tusks and horns, or a saw-toothed species with either, would refute the corresponding ban.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Dental and horn descriptions for carnivores, pigs, elephants, walrus, and horned ungulates.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: Character matrices that code tusks, horns, and tooth form together.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Skulls showing the teeth and horn cores for the same comparison.

obstacles: Tusk, horn, and saw-tooth each need a coding rule.
The universal scope is all viviparous quadrupeds, and the characters sit in species accounts rather than one trait file.
assessments.rationale: The forbidden combinations are observable on skulls and are already described for the familiar families. Building the cross-tabulation means harmonizing narrative accounts and matrix codings, not running a prepared column. That is a real but partial route: decisive for well-described genera, incomplete for every small mammal.

assessments.operationalization: Distinguish deciduous teeth from molars and score which tooth classes are replaced in humans, pigs, and other mammals; replacement of molars would refute the first universal, and any shed pig tooth would refute the pig clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Dental formulas and replacement notes, including elephants and pigs.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Juvenile and adult dentitions in which shed or replacing teeth can be seen.

obstacles: Shedding means replacement of deciduous teeth, not loss of worn teeth in old age.
Tooth-replacement series are not one downloadable table.
assessments.rationale: Species accounts record diphyodont replacement and the elephant pattern of molar succession, which are the comparisons that decide these universals. They are narrative and specimen-based rather than a single eruption table. A team can settle the main counterexamples; a complete mammal matrix would take longer to assemble.

assessments.operationalization: Measure tooth shade against age in horses and in other mammals, holding diet roughly fixed; darkening with age in horses, or whitening as the general mammalian pattern, would refute the stated contrast.
obstacles: Tooth color by age is not a field in the open trait or veterinary databases.
Diet and staining can mimic an age effect.
assessments.rationale: The contrast is measurable, and equine aging guides and small dental series discuss color, but those notes are scattered articles rather than a deposited table. No life-history database records shade. A test requires compiling those series and still has to separate stain from age, so only a weak version of the comparison can be attempted with what is public.

assessments.operationalization: Compare male and female dental formulas, not teeth retained into old age, in humans, sheep, goats, and pigs; equal formulas would refute a sex difference, and a higher male count in each species would support it.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Sex-typical dental formulas for humans and the three livestock species.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Male and female skulls of those species on which tooth classes can be counted.

candidate_datasets.name: ASM Mammal Diversity Database
candidate_datasets.role: Taxonomic backbone so that domestic breeds are not split into spurious species mid-count.

obstacles: Counts of teeth present in living adults confound formula with loss and impaction.
Breeds may differ from the species-typical formula.
assessments.rationale: The anatomical formula is recorded for these domestic species and can be checked on sexed skulls. Public dental surveys of living people measure remaining teeth, which is a different variable, so they should not be treated as the test. The four species are feasible as a specimen-and-account comparison, not as one sex-stratified download.

assessments.operationalization: Join species-typical tooth counts to maximum longevity and test the rank correlation after body size and phylogeny; a flat or negative relationship would refute the rule.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: Maximum longevity and adult body mass for the species being compared.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Dental formulas used as the tooth-count side of the join.

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: Body mass and life-history covariates that otherwise track both longevity and tooth number.

obstacles: Tooth counts have to be compiled onto the longevity table.
Body size and phylogeny move longevity and tooth number together.
assessments.rationale: Longevity is in a dedicated open database, and tooth counts exist in species accounts, so a joined analysis is possible for the mammals those sources share. The join is the work, and the biological confounders are serious: a raw correlation would not distinguish the claimed dental effect from size. The sentence is testable only as a phylogenetically controlled subset.

assessments.operationalization: For lizards, crocodiles, turtles, and frogs, score external ears, mammary glands, an intromittent organ, and external testes; presence of any of those structures in the group would refute the corresponding absence.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Accounts of ears, hemipenes or a penis, and reproductive anatomy for reptiles and amphibians.

candidate_datasets.name: AmphibiaWeb
candidate_datasets.role: Species accounts for frogs, including ear and reproductive structures.

candidate_datasets.name: AmphiBIO
candidate_datasets.role: Ecological and reproductive traits for amphibians as a coded complement to the narrative accounts.

obstacles: Frogs, lizards, crocodiles, and turtles do not share one body plan, so the four absences have to be scored separately.
Hemipenes and a crocodile or turtle penis are easy to miss in skeletal datasets.
assessments.rationale: Species accounts describe external ears, copulatory organs, and the lack of breasts for these groups, which is enough to test each clause on the main lineages. The four traits are not one matrix, and amphibian tables are stronger on ecology than on genital morphology. The claim is checkable family by family rather than by a single download.

assessments.operationalization: From GPS or radio tracks of Nile crocodiles, compare the fraction of daytime versus nighttime locations on land; more time in the water by day, or no day-night difference, would refute the rule.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: Crocodile tracking studies with timestamps that can be split into day and night and, where habitat is coded, land and water.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Timestamped observations as a rough check on when animals are seen ashore.

obstacles: Only a few Nile crocodile tracking studies are public.
Shoreline error can flip a wet-dry classification.
assessments.rationale: Diel habitat is measurable on existing tracks where land and water were distinguished. The public crocodile studies are few and geographically narrow relative to the species. The rule can be tested in those populations and should not be treated as already covered for river crocodiles in general.

assessments.operationalization: Pair night-time locations of Nile crocodiles with local air and water temperature; the explanation holds only if they are in the water on nights when the water is warmer than the air, and it fails if they enter water when the air is warmer or if temperature does not track the shift.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: Night locations of tracked crocodiles.

candidate_datasets.name: Copernicus Climate Data Store
candidate_datasets.role: ERA5 air temperature and water-temperature fields for the same nights and places.

obstacles: Gridded temperatures are not the microclimate against the animal's body.
A warmer river does not show that warmth is why the animal entered it.
assessments.rationale: Tracks and climate reanalysis can test the temperature fact that the explanation cites, at the scale of river and air rather than the animal's skin. They cannot separate warmth from foraging, safety, or habit as the reason for the move. The thermal clause is partly measurable; the causal 'because' remains confounded.

assessments.operationalization: Compare skin color with and without body inflation, holding temperature and background fixed; color change without inflation, or inflation without the stated color shift, would refute the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Natural-history description of color change in the common chameleon.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Photographs of color states, which do not record whether the body was inflated.

obstacles: The inflation trials sit in papers, not in a deposited experimental table.
Inflation, temperature, and disturbance can occur together, so a dark photograph does not identify the cause.
assessments.rationale: The mechanism predicts a specific manipulation, and species accounts plus photographs only document that the animal changes color. They do not pair color with measured inflation. Published experiments exist as papers rather than as an open trial archive, so a reanalysis can use them only by compiling methods and figures, which is a partial route.

assessments.operationalization: Proxy 'fly high' with aerial foraging or a high hand-wing index, then score toe count and toe arrangement; a high-flying species with other than four toes would refute the universal, and the wryneck should show two toes forward and two back.

candidate_datasets.name: EltonTraits 1.0
candidate_datasets.role: Foraging stratum, including aerial foragers, as a proxy for birds that fly high.

candidate_datasets.name: AVONET
candidate_datasets.role: Hand-wing index and primary lifestyle as a second flight proxy. Toe counts are not in this table.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Toe arrangements for the wryneck and for representative high-flying birds.

obstacles: Fly high is not a measured flight altitude.
Toe arrangement is not in the open bird-morphology matrices and has to be compiled.
assessments.rationale: Flight style is coded, and toe formula is not, so the join is only as good as compiled species accounts. The wryneck clause is a single-species check and is easier than the universal about high fliers. The analysis tests a proxy of the sentence on a subset of birds with described feet.

assessments.operationalization: Score fishes for a neck, paired limbs, testes, and mammary glands; testes or mammary tissue, or paired limbs rather than fins, would refute the matching clause, while absence of a tetrapod neck and of breasts would support those clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: Zebrafish anatomy ontology, including testes, kidneys, and fins, and lacking mammary glands.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: Taxonomy and morphology pages for bony and cartilaginous fishes.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Comparative accounts of fish gonads and the absence of breasts.

obstacles: Neck and limb need definitions that do not make those clauses true by vocabulary.
Zebrafish can refute a universal but is not a survey of every fish.
assessments.rationale: Testes and the absence of mammary glands are anatomical entries, not inferences, and a single well-annotated fish with testes refutes 'no testicles at all'. Neck and limb are the unstable words, because fins can be forced into or out of the limb category. The gonad and breast clauses are decidable now; the neck and limb clauses are only partly so.

assessments.operationalization: On dolphins, count mammary glands and record whether they open beside the genital slit rather than on the chest; a different count or a thoracic position would refute the anatomical claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Mammary anatomy and live birth for dolphins.

candidate_datasets.name: NOAA Fisheries species directory
candidate_datasets.role: Species pages for dolphins stating live birth and the position of the mammary slits.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: Life-history and morphology notes for delphinids.

obstacles: Dolphin covers several genera that share the same slit pattern.
Whether a slit counts as a teat is a minor coding choice.
assessments.rationale: The number and position of the mammary openings are stated in public species accounts for the animals the sentence names. The scope is narrow, so those accounts are adequate rather than a thin proxy. Checking two slits beside the genital opening is a direct reading of existing descriptions and specimens, not a new survey.

assessments.operationalization: Score fishes for olfactory organs and for an inner ear or otolith organ, not only for external ear flaps; either organ present refutes the claim that fishes lack both the organs and any passage for hearing and smell.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: Olfactory epithelium and ear structures in the zebrafish anatomical record.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: Curated presence of olfactory and otic characters across fishes.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: Species records, including otolith information linked from fish pages.

obstacles: An organ can be misread as an external opening only, which fishes lack for ears.
A zebrafish counterexample refutes the universal without covering every species.
assessments.rationale: Public anatomical databases list olfactory tissue and ear or otolith structures for fishes, which is the opposite of having neither organs nor passages. The universal is decided by those presences even though most species lack a full anatomical annotation. External nostrils and ear openings are a different reading, and the rationale for scoring should keep internal organs in the test because the sentence denies the organs themselves.

assessments.operationalization: Cross reproductive mode with bony versus cartilaginous fishes, and check the anglerfish separately; a viviparous scaly fish, or an egg-laying cartilaginous fish, refutes the matching universal, and the anglerfish is scored against the stated exception.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: Class and reproductive guild for bony and cartilaginous fishes, including Lophius.

candidate_datasets.name: Sharkipedia
candidate_datasets.role: Reproductive mode across sharks and rays, the cartilaginous side of the table.

obstacles: Scaly has to be coded so that scaleless bony fishes are not silently dropped or silently included.
The fishing-frog is the anglerfish Lophius, a bony fish, so the exception is not inside the cartilaginous group.
assessments.rationale: Reproductive guild and higher taxon are standard fields covering most fishes, which is the stated scope. The two universals can be cross-tabulated directly, and the anglerfish has its own species record. Ordinary database queries are enough to confirm or refute both clauses.

assessments.operationalization: Inspect adult cattle and horse hearts for an ossified element; a bone in some ox hearts and in the horse would support the claim, and no such bone in a broad adult sample of either would refute it.
obstacles: The heart bone is a soft-tissue element and is not in skeletal repositories or life-history tables.
It is reported as dependent on age and breed, so a few hearts would not settle the 'not in every ox' clause.
assessments.rationale: The observation is anatomically specific and would be settled by a series of hearts, but those series are veterinary papers and teaching collections rather than a public imaging dataset. Skeletal archives do not substitute, because the element is inside the heart. The claim is testable from compiled pathology notes for a few breeds and not from an open download.

assessments.operationalization: Score gall-bladder presence in deer, roe, horse, mule, ass, seals, and pigs; a gall bladder in horse or deer would refute those clauses, and universal absence in all pigs would refute the 'some kinds' hedge.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Visceral notes for horses, deer, pigs, and seals, including the gall bladder when the account mentions it.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: Curated presence or absence of the gall bladder where the literature has been encoded.

obstacles: Gall-bladder presence is not a column in the mammal life-history tables.
Pigs and seals vary by species, so the hedge requires a species-level map.
assessments.rationale: The organ is a yes-no anatomical fact, and species accounts plus curated phenotype records cover the named domestic and game mammals unevenly. Mule and ass can be tied to the horse, while seals and the pig exception need species-by-species notes. A compilation can test the list; it is not already a column.

assessments.operationalization: In a sample of stags, count dipteran larvae in the retropharyngeal pouch and test whether every animal has a cluster near twenty; any uninfected stag, or a typical count far from twenty, refutes the corresponding clause.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Observations of deer nasal-bot flies, which show that the parasite exists but not how many larvae each stag carries.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Host and parasite notes for deer where bots are mentioned.

obstacles: No open dataset gives larval counts in the head across stag populations.
'Without exception' and 'about twenty' are stronger than a presence record.
assessments.rationale: Presence of deer bot flies is documentable from observations and host notes. Prevalence and a count near twenty, required by the wording, are not in those sources. Parasitology surveys exist as papers rather than as a maintained prevalence table, so the universal and the number stay only partly approachable.

assessments.operationalization: Score kidneys and a urinary bladder in fishes and birds; either organ in either group refutes the universal for that organ.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: Zebrafish kidney records, a direct counterexample class for fishes.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Bird and fish accounts that state the kidney and whether a urinary bladder is present.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: Curated renal and bladder characters for vertebrates.

obstacles: The urinary bladder must be kept distinct from a swim bladder.
Annotated model species and species accounts refute a universal without listing every species.
assessments.rationale: Kidneys of fishes and birds are standard anatomical entries in public databases, so a universal denial is decidable without new dissection. The bladder half is also described, with birds lacking a urinary bladder and possessing kidneys, which splits the two organs. The test is a presence query on existing annotations, not a proxy.

assessments.operationalization: For horned mammals that lack upper incisors, count stomach chambers and code cud-chewing; a count other than four, or cud-chewing without that dentition, would challenge the link the sentence draws.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Dentition, horn, stomach, and rumination notes for cattle, sheep, deer, and camelids.

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: Diet and taxonomy for the same ungulates, as a frame for which species are horned grazers.

obstacles: Camelids chew the cud with a three-chambered stomach, so four chambers and rumination are not the same trait.
Stomach-chamber counts are in species accounts rather than in PanTHERIA.
assessments.rationale: The dental and horn conditions and the stomach layout are described for the main ruminant families. They are not one coded matrix, and camelids show why chamber number and cud-chewing should be scored separately. A family-level compilation can test the rule; it is not a finished download.

assessments.operationalization: Count ribs or rib-bearing precloacal vertebrae on snake skeletal CT; a typical count near thirty would support the claim, and counts far above thirty would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Snake microCT volumes on which vertebrae and ribs can be counted.

candidate_datasets.name: DigiMorph
candidate_datasets.role: Additional reptile skeletal reconstructions for the same count.
